Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For a Milan side capable of dismantling Chivu’s team with three goals in 45 minutes, the Ferencváros game should pose no real concern. It must, however, be approached with focus and a significant yet carefully considered rotation of the squad.

The situation mirrors the league campaign in one key respect: the table. By winning on Saturday, Milan got back into the hunt for the Scudetto, so a similar result is needed in Europe. The Rossoneri currently sit on three points, while the Hungarians have a perfect record of nine.

Even with a win, Milan won’t catch their opponents, but they will improve their position in the table which is a necessity, especially with only four games left after this.

Ferencvaros’ position in the standings is the result of a long, arduous journey. They began their Europa League campaign in the first qualifying round, eliminating Serbia’s Vojvodina.

In the second round, they knocked out the Dutch side Twente. They then triumphed over Poland’s Górnik Zabrze in the third round, before defeating Trabzonspor in the play-offs.

All that hard work has paid off in the league phase, where they have secured three wins out of three – against Celtic, Plzeň and Torreense – making them one of only five teams with a perfect record. The others are Benfica, Leverkusen, Bournemouth and Olympiacos.

Two of these four have already faced the Rossoneri, which speaks to the challenging nature of Milan’s schedule. Against the Portuguese side, Amorim faltered in his debut, fielding a side packed with reserves in a high-profile match.

Against Bournemouth, the result was compromised by two penalties and Mike Maignan’s red card. In between, there was a resounding victory in Salzburg, spearheaded by Alphadjo Cissé. This explains why they currently sit on just three points, a situation that now demands a turnaround.

The upcoming schedule is relatively more manageable, featuring an away trip to Athens, a home match against Sunderland, a visit to Sofia to face Levski, and a game against Ararat Armenia in Milan.

Securing a spot in the round of 16 is a task that needs to be completed, and preferably soon. Sitting on three points in 24th place, Milan’s current standing in the Europa League does not reflect the goal the club have set for themselves: to go all the way in the competition.

Cisse will return to the starting line-up for the competition in which he is the team’s top scorer: three goals, all netted on the same night in Austria. The squad will once again be adjusted to accommodate the turnover and rotations necessary for managing resources.

This time, the team are better prepared to absorb these changes after welcoming back some players before the derby. Consequently, there will be further rotation on Thursday night, with the aim of keeping everyone fresh.

A change is unavoidable in goal, where the suspension for the captain Maignan will see Lorenzo Torriani make his first start. In defence, Sankhoun Diawara could play centrally, while Pervis Estupinan or Davide Bartesaghi (or both, with the latter pushed further forward) could feature on the left.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will take on a Modrić-like role, while the versatile Filippo Terracciano could slot in as a mezzala (or even at right-back, covering for Mario Gila). There is also a chance of seeing the very young Christian Comotto in action.

In attack, Omari Hutchinson is a certain starter:he looked lively during his time on the pitch against Bologna and performed even better against Udinese, a match in which he scored his first goal for Milan. Cisse could lead the line, but Francesco Camarda and Goncalo Ramos remain candidates too.

#2040. Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Joe Westley believes his battle for game time with fellow Dundee attackers will only benefit the Tayside club.

With just one defeat in the last five, the Dark Blues are in fifth place in the William Hill Premiership and the fourth-highest scorers, with Ashley Hay notching three in the last four games and Bradley Fink with four in the last six.

Westley missed three games with an ankle injury but replaced Fink in the 3-1 win over Kilmarnock last Wednesday and, ahead of the Tayside derby against St Johnstone at McDiarmid Park on Saturday, the 22-year-old, with five goals in all competitions this season, said: “I think it’s a healthy competition.

“Everyone wants to be playing football and be in the team. So when we’ve got Ash and Brad scoring, it means I need to up my game and score as many as I can when I’m given the chance because you know that when you’ve got the shirt, people are waiting to take it off you.

“It’s a healthy competition and I think we all drive each other to be the best versions of ourselves.

“I think when all the strikers are scoring and doing well, it’s good to be a part of an attack that’s doing well because you create for each other. If everyone’s firing and everyone’s doing well, then it increases your chance of getting goals and assisting as well.

“It’s a really good time to be an attacker at the club. I think it’s starting to click between everyone and whoever’s on up front has got a great understanding of what’s wanted from them. It gives them the best possible chance to score goals and win games.

“I think everything can come down to hard work. As a group everyone around the club works so hard day in, day out and we’re pushed in training, we’re pushed in the gym and I think we try and always gain the little one percent that we can every week.

“But also there’s the environment that the manager has created where everyone’s in it together. Everyone wants to do the hard yards for each other and I think the hard yards and the basics of football are things that can separate you from other teams in the league.

“I think so far this season we’ve been good at the basics and as long as we continue to do them we’ll be fine.”

The hosts are under the new management of Karl Robinson, who inherits a side sat bottom of League One, while their visitors are in their own battle at the bottom end of League Two.

Bromley will set out to make a winning start to life under Karl Robinson in their first FA Cup game of the campaign on Saturday after a tough start to 2026-27.

In a memorable season last time around, they earned automatic promotion from League Two, but the Ravens failed to carry their momentum into the new season with two-time promotion-winning manager Andy Woodman departing in October after overseeing 10 league games in which his side managed eight points.

They were unable to bounce back under the temporary care of Byron Webster, only managing a draw against Peterborough United before 4-1 and 3-2 away losses to MK Dons and Wigan Athletic respectively last week.

That leaves the Ravens bottom of the third tier with nine points on the board, having scored just 13 goals in 13 games and conceded 33 - 10 more than any other team in the division.

Now on the back of the midweek appointment of Karl Robinson as their new manager, who will be tasked with maintaining their third-tier status this term, Bromley will hope to make a winning start to progress in the cup.

Their visitors, meanwhile, are also seeking a confidence-boosting cup win to lift spirits in the midst of a tough campaign.

Rotherham United swapped places with their hosts last season, suffering a second relegation in three seasons to drop to League Two.

They began the term under the new management of Alex Bruce and are yet to reverse their fortunes, currently sitting 22nd on just 12 points from 12 games having won two and lost six of those while conceding 25 - the second most in the league.

With pressure growing at the AESSEAL New York Stadium, as they now only lead the League Two relegation on goal difference in the midst of their rut, Rotherham United will be desperate to put a win on the board on Saturday when they turn to cup action against new third-tier opposition.

Rotherham United will likely remain without Ossama Ashley, Jamie Jellis, Fabio Tavares and Marvin Kaleta on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Defenders Dominic Iorfa and Jili Buyabu were sent off in last week's loss to Swindon but are available in the FA Cup, while Kian Spence was also back involved in midweek after a suspension.

Paul Mullin and Tom Bradshaw will both compete to come back into the attack from the outset, with the former having scored eight league goals so far this season.

#2035. Raphinha responds to Flick fears after Ancelotti talks

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 22:12

Barcelona captain Raphinha has moved to ease Hansi Flick's concerns over his upcoming international commitments, revealing that he has already discussed his fitness and playing time with Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti.

The 29-year-old, who signed a contract extension until June 2030 on Thursday, admitted that he is still not fully fit after suffering another muscular problem while representing his country earlier this season.

His comments come just days after Flick publicly questioned the demands of another lengthy international trip, particularly given that Raphinha returned injured from Brazil's previous training camp.

However, the former Leeds United attacker insists that Ancelotti understands his situation and will take his recovery into account during November's friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

The reassurance comes at an important time for Barcelona, with Raphinha enjoying the most prolific start to a season of his career and several demanding fixtures approaching.

Speaking to reporters following the announcement of his new Barcelona contract, Raphinha addressed the concerns surrounding his participation in Brazil's upcoming matches.

The forward confirmed that he had already spoken with Ancelotti about his physical condition and the importance of managing his workload.

"Ancelotti, as a coach, knows he has to distribute playing time," Raphinha explained, as quoted by Barca Blaugranes.

"He knows that an injury would be complicated for Brazil too, and he knows how to manage minutes.

"We've spoken; he knows I'm recovering from an injury. I'm fine, but not 100%. Barça fans shouldn't worry because I'm taking good care of myself."

The admission that he has yet to regain full fitness is particularly significant given his recent injury history.

Raphinha suffered a hamstring problem during Brazil's international commitments in October, forcing him to return to Barcelona for treatment.

The setback ruled him out of two club matches, adding to concerns surrounding a player who has experienced several muscular injuries over the past year.

He also suffered an injury while representing Brazil against France in March, subsequently missing Barcelona's Champions League quarter-final against Atletico Madrid.

Another physical problem during the 2026 World Cup prevented him from featuring in the latter stages of Brazil's campaign.

Those setbacks explain why Flick was uneasy about the forward undertaking another long-distance journey so soon after his latest recovery.

Speaking on October 30, the Barcelona manager acknowledged that he had discussed Raphinha's situation with sporting director Deco.

"After the last international break, he came back injured, which wasn't ideal," Flick explained.

The German coach also made it clear that he would welcome a cautious approach from Brazil's coaching staff.

"If he can manage his playing time well, I'll be happy. Travelling to Singapore isn't ideal, but it's beyond my control."

The comments reflected Barcelona's concern over the demands of international football rather than any suggestion that Raphinha should abandon his commitments to Brazil.

Ancelotti's side are scheduled to face Japan on November 14 before meeting Singapore three days later, with both fixtures taking place in Singapore.

Raphinha's latest remarks offer some reassurance that his condition has been discussed with the Brazil manager, although he did not disclose any specific agreement regarding the number of minutes he will play.

The timing of the international break is especially sensitive for Barcelona because of Raphinha's extraordinary influence this season.

The Brazilian has scored 19 goals in just 13 appearances across all competitions, including 15 in La Liga and four in the Champions League.

His performances have helped Flick's side establish themselves at the top of the Spanish league, while his adaptation to a more central attacking role has made him an even greater threat in front of goal.

Previously deployed primarily on the wing, Raphinha has increasingly operated as a centre-forward, taking advantage of his movement and finishing ability inside the penalty area.

His form was rewarded on Thursday when Barcelona officially confirmed a contract extension keeping him at Camp Nou until June 2030.

The agreement provides further evidence of his importance to the club, particularly after a period in which his future had previously been the subject of transfer speculation.

However, Barcelona's immediate priority will be ensuring that their captain remains available during a demanding period of the campaign.

Flick's side travel to Atletico Madrid on Sunday for a crucial La Liga encounter, with only two points separating the clubs at the top of the standings.

They also have a Champions League meeting with Manchester City to negotiate after the international break, increasing the importance of Raphinha returning from Brazil without another setback.

The forward's situation presents a delicate balancing act for both managers.

Ancelotti will want to make use of one of Brazil's most productive attacking players, while Flick is understandably reluctant to risk losing a footballer who has become central to Barcelona's ambitions.

Read more: After missing out on another senior call-up, my Celtic form has been rewarded

“We were shouting from the rooftops that they needed a right-winger. There’s no right-winger either. Why did they keep Cerny on today? How did he last so long? He gets a bit more motivated in this game because of some past incidents.

“There’s an incident, I don’t know if you remember, Cerny was playing for Glasgow Rangers. Glasgow Rangers score a goal against Celtic, Cerny pulled a water bottle from the bench and sprayed it at the Celtic fans. That’s why he was booed every time the ball came to his feet.

“He was booed not only because he played for Rangers, but also because of that incident. But Besiktas’ flaws have now been revealed.”

#2032. SC Paderborn vs Eintracht Frankfurt - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 05 Nov 2026 22:17

Hoping to distance themselves from the Bundesliga's relegation zone, SC Paderborn will welcome European hopefuls Eintracht Frankfurt to Home Deluxe Arena on Saturday.

The hosts are searching for their second win in six games, while Die Adler could earn a third on the bounce.

Ralf Kettemann's Paderborn have performed admirably since making the step up from the second division, but they will be looking over their shoulder ahead of a tough challenge this weekend.

Saturday's hosts are currently 14th in the Bundesliga with nine points, sitting just two above 16th-placed Union Berlin in the relegation playoff spot.

Last time out, Kettemann's side were held to a 0-0 draw by Borussia Monchengladbach, failing to score for the second successive match.

In fact, only Schalke 04 have netted fewer than Paderborn's six goals in the German top flight this season, a concerning trait that the manager will be need to address in order to stave off the threat of demotion.

That being said, the promoted club have maintained an impressive defensive record so far, with Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich the only teams to have conceded less than their nine in eight matches.

Another positive for the hosts is the fact a win could lift them into the top half, considering they are level on points with every club up to 10th-placed Augsburg, and are just one behind ninth-placed Mainz 05.

Meanwhile, Adi Hutter's Frankfurt have been inconsistent for the majority of the 2026-27 campaign so far, though the club will be keen to prove they have turned a corner.

Die Adler beat Hamburger SV 3-1 at home last time out, and by the same score away in the DFB-Pokal just days earlier, marking the first time they have recorded back-to-back wins this season.

That latest success has Hutter's men eighth with 11 points, just two shy of sixth-placed Bayer Leverkusen in the race for Europe.

Heading into Saturday's showdown, Frankfurt have now won three of their last four outings across all competitions, only succumbing to a 1-0 defeat at Dortmund on October 24.

However, the visitors have come out on top in just one of their four Bundesliga away games this term - downing Mainz 3-1 in mid-September - while conceding 11 goals in the process.

Eintracht Frankfurt form (all competitions):

Paderborn will be without Marcel Hoffmeier due to a thigh injury, as well as fellow centre-back Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant, who returned to training late last month but is still building fitness after a lengthy layoff.

In their absence, Tjark Scheller, Mattes Hansen and Jano ter Horst look set to start in Kettemann's three-man defence, flanked by wing-backs Laurin Curda and Raphael Obermair.

Elsewhere, midfielder Timur Gayret remains sidelined with a knee injury, though Santiago Castaneda, Tom Baack and Gabriel Vidovic should be on hand to operate in the centre of the park.

As for Frankfurt, they are missing long-term absentee Jessic Ngankam, who is continuing his recovery from a thigh injury, while attacking midfielder Mario Gotze is a doubt due to an ear infection that caused him to miss training on Wednesday and Thursday.

With that in mind, striker Jonathan Burkardt will be supported by a trio of Ritsu Doan, Can Uzun and Fares Chaibi on Saturday.

There are also question marks bout the fitness of centre-half Robin Koch, who only trained partially this week after picking up a knock to his knee, but Lilian Brassier and Jeremiaha Maluze will be ready to line up at the heart of Hutter's defence if he is unavailable.

Noll; Scheller, Hansen, Ter Horst; Curda, Vidovic, Baack, Castaneda, Obermair; Tigges, Marino

Frankfurt will be buoyed by their improved results in recent weeks, though they will need to defy their form on the road to secure all three points, so expect to see a close-fought game.

#2028. Barnsley vs Aldershot Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:18, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:00

Aldershot Town will set out to pull off an FA Cup first-round upset in South Yorkshire on Saturday, when they visit Oakwell to take on third-tier Barnsley.

The hosts enter at this stage while their visitors took part in the final qualifying round and needed a replay to progress.

Barnsley head into FA Cup action for the first time this season on Saturday in need of a victory to arrest a slump in the early stages of 2026-27.

The Reds reached the third round of this competition last year, falling in a trip to Liverpool, but begin their new campaign with just four wins from 17 competitive matches so far this term with all of those coming in the first six outings.

They did enjoy a positive start to life back under returning boss Daniel Stendel but are now winless in 11 games since early September, losing nine of those including four straight league defeats heading into the weekend.

Stendel's men were, at least, able to end that rut at home to Oxford United on Saturday, drawing 1-1 thanks to Vimal Yoganathan's opener having been down to 10 men inside 10 minutes, but the South Yorkshire side still sit 23rd in League One with just nine points on the board from 12 games having conceded 22 goals.

With positives to take from the weekend's display but real cause for concern around their recent months, Barnsley will be desperate to avoid an upset at the weekend and taste victory at Oakwell.

Their opponents, meanwhile, make the trip north having scraped through the final qualifying round in the FA Cup.

Aldershot Town entered this year's competition in the fourth and final round of qualifying, taking on ninth-tier Tadley Calleva, but they were only able to draw 2-2 at home before prevailing in a 2-0 triumph on the road in the replay.

That eventual cup win broke up a five-game losing run in the National League for the Shots, who also headed into the weekend in the midst of a rut, but they bounced back to winning ways at home to Gateshead, as Brody Peart scored the only goal inside five minutes.

Scott Davies's side climbed back up to 14th spot in the fifth tier with that result, and now on the back of a midweek National League Cup loss to Ipswich Town Under-21s, they will hope to defy the odds at Oakwell on Saturday to reach the FA Cup second round for just the second time since 2015.

Barnsley are set to remain without attackers Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Stendel should field a near full-strength XI with the Reds desperate for a win to turn their fortunes round, meaning star man Reyes Cleary should continue on the wing, while Tobi Adeyemo was injured early on Saturday and may be replaced up front by Rylan Brownlie.

Veteran and recent signing Daniel Johnson may be afforded a start in midfield alongside either Luca Connell or Patrick Kelly, while Jack Shepherd is available at the back despite being sent off last time out in the league.

Aldershot Town will field a similar starting XI from last week's league win over Gateshead.

Marcus Dinanga and Marcus Wyllie will both hope to start in attack, but if they continue with a 4-2-3-1 shape the line should again be led by Tristan Abrahams, who has scored six goals so far this season.

A summer of plenty of change added several key men to their ranks, with Michael Stickland and Kiki Oshilaja now mainstays in defence and Dominic Odusanya and Conor Lawless likely to continue a midfield partnership if the latter is fit having been forced off last weekend.

Slicker; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche; Connell, Johnson; Yoganathan, McGeegan, Cleary; Brownlie

Hayes; Stickland, Oshilaja, Dyce, Harfield; Lawless, Odusanya; Peart, Tuma, Sandah; Abrahams

Barnsley could certainly be vulnerable to a cup upset at home, given their poor league record and struggles at both ends of the pitch and growing concern around the club, but needing a win to start turning their form around, we do expect Stendel's men to outclass their non-league visitors.

#2026. Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

Spain should withdraw as co-hosts of the 2030 World Cup if Morocco is awarded the right to stage the final, the European nation’s main opposition party leader has said.

The centenary finals are set to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal, with the opening three matches due to be staged in South America as a nod to Uruguay’s hosting of the inaugural tournament in 1930.

FIFA has not confirmed which of the three main co-hosts will be awarded the final, only saying that a decision will be taken in due course.

However, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the opposition People’s Party, insists Spain should back out of hosting the tournament if it is not chosen to stage the final.

“If Morocco ends up hosting the final, Spain should leave the organisation (of the tournament),” he told El Chiringuito TV.

He added on X in a post quoting the El Chiringuito interview: “Restoring our country’s pride also means not letting anyone walk all over us.

“The World Cup final belongs to Spain. The world’s top footballing nation is not humiliated. I will defend my country’s interests. In this too.”

The revamped Bernabeu Stadium or Camp Nou would be worthy contenders to host, but Morocco are continuing to push for the Grande Stade Hassan II in Casablanca, with a projected capacity of 115,000, to stage the showpiece game.

Morocco is currently staging the Under-17 boy’s World Cup, held an emergency meeting of the FIFA management board in August when FIFA president Gianni Infantino looked under threat and will also be the venue for next year’s FIFA Congress, where Infantino is hoping to secure a fourth term as president.

Aiming to continue their climb up the Championship table and break into the playoff places, Sheffield United will head to The Valley to take on Charlton Athletic on Saturday.

Charlton Athletic return to action at the weekend aiming to end a dismal run of Championship form and arrest a drop towards the relegation zone.

Following a 19th-placed finish in their first season back in the second tier last time around, the Addicks won their first three league matches of the new term but have since drawn five and lost six of 11 matches.

In those games, Nathan Jones's side have scored just six goals and conceded 20, dropping to 21st spot in the process, just one place and four points above Burnley in the drop zone.

They have now suffered four straight defeats heading into their final match before the international break, falling to Watford, Norwich City and Middlesbrough before they hosted newly-promoted Bolton Wanderers on Tuesday and again came away empty-handed as Sam Dalby scored the only goal inside 20 minutes at the Valley.

With pressure surely growing on Jones, and the international break arguably coming at a decent time to arrest Charlton's slump, they will be desperate to put a win on the board to increase their lead over the drop zone ahead of the return to action.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to London aiming to carry an upturn in form into the break.

Unlike the hosts, Sheffield United are now bouncing back from a slow start to the Championship season, having set out to challenge for promotion this term only to pick up just nine points from their first eight matches before the opening break of the season.

Chris Wilder's men have reversed their fortunes since, though, putting 13 more points on the board in six outings courtesy of four wins and a draw alongside a solitary away defeat to Portsmouth.

Following a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham on Friday, the Blades headed to strugglers Preston North End on Tuesday and came from 1-0 down to win 3-2 thanks to Sydie Peck's first-half hat-trick, leaving them on 22 points from 14 matches with just five teams conceding fewer than the 17 goals they have allowed.

Now in a much better position in ninth spot, and just one point behind eighth-placed West Ham United, Sheffield United will look to make it three straight wins with the chance to head into the second break of the campaign in the playoff places.

Charlton Athletic remain unable to call on winger Rob Apter, who has been sidelined since early September.

In their midweek defeat, Jones replaced midfielder Nathaniel Chalobah with attacker Miles Leaburn at half time and could go with a more attacking shape from the outset at the weekend with Leaburn, Matt Godden, Sonny Carey and Millenic Alli all competing for attacking spots.

That is after Charlie Kelman led the line against Bolton with support from Harvey Knibbs, Karlan Grant and top scorer Tyreece Campbell, while Conor Coventry is a mainstay in the engine room and Will Mannion was preferred in net over Arthur Okonkwo last time out.

Sheffield United are without forwards Patrick Bamford and Ryan One and midfielder Joe Rothwell, while Kalvin Phillips was also absent in midweek but may be fit to feature.

He is unlikely to be rushed back, though, and Wilder should field a similar starting XI from their midweek away win, meaning Jairo Riedewald may again partner Peck, who decided that game with his hat-trick, while Liam Kitching should come straight back into the defence after serving a one-match suspension on Tuesday.

In a 4-4-2 shape, they may again be flanked by Romelle Donovan and Tahith Chong with Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Tyrese Campbell and Oliver Arblaster competing for attacking spots in Bamford's absence.

Charlton Athletic possible starting lineup:

Mannion; McNamara, Jones, Koumetio, Bell; Coventry; Alli, Knibbs, Grant, Campbell; Leaburn

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Chong, Peck, Riedewald, Donovan; Brereton Diaz, Cannon

Sheffield United appear to be hitting their stride since the season's first international break and have ground out several hard-fought wins in recent weeks, while the hosts seem unable to arrest a slump and we fancy Wilder's men to take all three points again with their sights set on the top eight.

#2024. GdS: Milan score, Ramos struggles – the paradox that Amorim must fix

As the weeks go by Ruben Amorim continues to tweak AC Milan tactically, but a constant theme remains: Goncalo Ramos can’t score consistently.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan are evolving on an almost game-by-game basis, but the only one who remains the same is Ramos. One factor stands out above all: the Portuguese fails to get into the flow of play, not only when the team is struggling but even when they play well and win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His derby stats tragically mirror those reported the previous Wednesday against Bologna: zero shots on target, zero shots off target, zero blocked shots, zero chances created, zero assists. The same story. Even the number of balls played was identical: 31.

Yet they were two very different games. Against Inter, Gonçalo even infuriated Luka Modric, who shortly after the quarter-hour mark unleashed a sharp, angled right-footer that was aimed squarely at Josep Martinez. Ramos was right in the path of the ball, potentially denying a 3-0 goal.

Modric muttered words of frustration under his breath, knowing of course that it was not deliberate sabotage. That incident is proof that there are times when nothing goes right, not even when everyone else is playing with a smile.

Ramos’s first two months resemble Gimenez’s a year ago: just as Santiago couldn’t score but had Massimiliano Allegri’s trust thanks to his backroom work for the team, the same is true for Gonçalo. Unlike Santiago, he has scored three goals, though one was a penalty and one a gift.

In terms of goalscoring, his contribution is completely inadequate compared to expectations, the player’s level, and the club’s investment in bringing him to Milanello. Ramos runs, he battles and he tries to get the team moving forward but he can’t get fully involved.

You can also look at it from the other angle: is it the team that are incapable of giving him service? Perhaps precisely because he’s a striker who roams widely and provides no reference points not only for opposing defenders, but also for his own team-mates.

In any case, he was and remains the starting centre-forward. Partly because Francesco Camarda – in Amorim’s eyes – clearly doesn’t offer enough guarantees, and partly because of Gonçalo’s dirty work, which serves to free up space for others.

It’s no coincidence that Adrien Rabiot is frequently finding the back of the net, and the same goes for Diego Moreira and Alphadjo Cisse, all players who don’t usually hang around in the box.

Furthermore, Milan have recently developed a particular quality: when their shots hit the target, they end up in the back of the net. The two goals against Bologna came with their first two shots, the three against Inter with their first three.

Between the Emilians and the Nerazzurri, Milan have had a total of seven shots on target, squeezing five goals from them: a stratospheric 71%. The million-dollar question, now that Milan are poised for the Scudetto race, is: if Ramos were to unlock himself, how far can this team go?

#2023. Michael Carrick hits back at suspicions that he is on the brink of the sack at Man United - and insists he is relishing Tuesday's battle against Roma

Published: 10:06 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 10:07 EDT, 2 November 2026

Michael Carrick doesn’t feel like he is on his last legs as Manchester United head coach – but admits people might think he is ‘crazy’ for looking forward to the Champions League clash with Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday night.

Speaking ahead of the game at Carrington on Monday, Carrick also insisted that he has no concerns over Lisandro Martinez’s commitment despite the Argentine’s reckless red card at Chelsea on Saturday.

United go into the game against Roma in danger of equalling a club record of ten consecutive games without a win in a single season set by Dave Sexton’s team in March 1978.

Last week, United bosses gave Carrick more time to turn the season, but there is a growing suspicion that he could be sacked in the international break after the next two games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Asked if he has the same feeling, Carrick said: ‘No, not at all. Listen. I can’t look into the future, and you never know what's going to happen. I don't know what's going to happen.

‘That doesn't change the way I feel. That doesn't change how we're preparing for the game tomorrow, and I'm actually really looking forward to the game. I can't wait for the game tomorrow.

Michael Carrick does not feel like he is on the brink of the sack at Manchester United

'You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I genuinely, really can't wait for the game tomorrow, and that's all I'm focused on, really I am.

‘Whatever happens, it is going to happen, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first.

‘It's what I am, it's what I live for, you know. A lot of people could do my job when you're winning a lot of football games. It's about finding the solutions, finding the answers, staying strong, leading right and getting the best out of the players.

‘We've got to keep pushing for that. But it doesn't change my mindset at all. I love being here, I love working with the players, and the struggles and the challenges, that just drives you on to want it even more.’

Martinez is available to face Roma but will be banned for the Villa game on Sunday after he was sent off for two bookings in the space of 82 seconds at Stamford Bridge – earning the second yellow card for striking Wesley Fofana in the face.

It followed the Argentine’s outburst against club bosses, and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular, after United were beaten by Atletico Madrid last month.

However, Carrick insisted there are no concerns over Martinez’s commitment or the general discipline in the dressing-room after Bruno Fernandes criticised his tactics in the defeat to Como a fortnight ago.

‘No, I've got no concerns about commitment at all,’ said Carrick. ‘Things happen in football. Sometimes you do things, sometimes you make a decision, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you. But the commitment is not an issue for sure.

‘The dressing room is a good, good place, so perceptions are a funny thing. They can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things. I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don't question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment's not a thing at all.’

He says he is excited for Tuesday's Champions League clash against Roma - despite the potential for another embarrassment

Martinez and Fernandes are out of contract in June, although United have an option to extend both by 12 months. They are in talks with Fernandes but Martinez faces a more uncertain future at Old Trafford.

‘You know how discussions go and when anything's finalised, we'll let you know. But at this stage, there's nothing any further to update really,’ said Carrick.

Patrick Dorgu returned to training at Carrington on Monday after six weeks out of action but the Dane won’t be involved against Roma. Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford missed the session and will remain on the sidelines with Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte.

United badly need a win after picking up three points from their first three games against Sabah, Atletico Madrid and Como. They sit 20th in the league phase. After Roma, they face Sporting Lisbon, RB Leipzig, Bayern Munich and Villarreal.

‘Of course we're looking for the win,’ said Carrick. ‘There is the bigger picture and it’s about getting through to the later stages. One or two games you can get away with really, as long as you make amends for that. Tomorrow and the games coming up are going to dictate that for us. So we're certainly still in it with a great chance of progressing, and it's got to be the focus for now.’

Roma’s only defeat in all competitions this season came in a dramatic 4-3 collapse to Real Madrid in the Champions League. But they have lost on all four of their visits to Old Trafford including a 7-1 defeat in 2007 – when Carrick scored twice – and 6-2 in 2021.

‘Long time ago, eh?’ smiled Carrick. ‘It was a magical night, I have to say. It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I've been fortunate enough to witness.

‘So the fact that I scored a couple and that was very unusual gives me great, great memories. But it was more the whole emotion of the night really. I have to say that it was a special one.’

#2022. Minnesota United vs San Jose Earthquakes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 05 Nov 2026 22:31, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:18

Minnesota United and San Jose Earthquakes draw the curtain on their 2026 Major League Soccer regular season campaign when they lock horns at Allianz Field on Sunday morning.

While the home side head into the league finale needing maximum points to stand a chance of securing back-to-back playoff appearances, San Jose will aim to finish the campaign strong and gather momentum ahead of the post-season quest.

A strong showing at the business end of the season has put Minnesota United in contention for playoff qualification ahead of a crunch final-day showdown, with the Loons securing a 3-1 win over Los Angeles FC on Monday to maintain their newfound form.

Joaquin Pereyra turned in an eye-catching display at the BMO Stadium, netting on either side of Cherrion Valerius’s 34th-minute strike to put the visitors three goals up, before Sergio Vasquez pulled one back for Los Angeles FC in the 89th minute.

Coming off a 3-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City on October 29, Minnesota United have now picked up three wins in their most recent four outings and are unbeaten in six straight matches (3W 3D), having lost each of the five games preceding this run.

This late-season resurgence has seen Cameron Knowles’s men surge into 12th place in the Western Conference standings with 41 points from 33 matches, just two points behind ninth-placed Colorado Rapids in the final playoff qualifying spot.

Attacking improvements have been integral in Minnesota’s upturn in form, with 2+ goals scored in five of their last six games, and they will also hope to make home advantage count against an opposing side who have failed to win their last six league visits to Allianz Field, losing four and claiming two draws since a 3-1 victory in May 2018.

Having seen their form take a dip in recent weeks, San Jose Earthquakes finally rediscovered their winning touch last Saturday when they held on to see out a 2-1 victory over Real Salt Lake and record their first victory since late September.

In an action-packed first half at PayPal Park, Ousseni Bouda and Benjamin Kikanovic netted in a 15-minute spell to put the Quakes in a commanding lead, and after Juan Sanabria halved the deficit with a 23rd-minute strike, the home side did well to repel Real Salt Lake and leave with all three points.

Prior to that, San Jose saw their nine-game unbeaten league streak come to an end on October 25, when they were hammered 3-0 by FC Dallas at the Toyota Stadium, four days before playing out a 2-2 stalemate with Colorado Rapids on home turf.

After enduring a disappointing 2025 campaign that saw them finish 10th in the West and narrowly miss out on the playoffs, Bruce Arena’s men have enjoyed a significant turnaround this season, collecting 52 points from 33 games to sit third in the conference standings, three points behind second-placed Dallas.

With playoff qualification already assured, San Jose will be keen to finish the regular season on a high, but a run of just one win in eight matches since August suggests they still have work to do before the campaign concludes.

San Jose Earthquakes Major League Soccer form:

American youngster Kayne Rizvanovich was left out of the team list against Los Angeles FC last time out, and the 19-year-old goalkeeper is also expected to sit out this weekend's matchup.

Kelvin Yeboah has been a standout performer for Minnesota this season, and the Italian striker, who has racked up 18 goals and four assists in 29 league starts, will be one to keep an eye on.

#2021. Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

Thomas Tuchel says Cole Palmer is paying the price for his controversial withdrawal from England’s last camp.

The Chelsea forward was a notable omission from Tuchel’s squad for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

He was originally named in Tuchel’s group for September and October’s matches but withdrew due to a minor injury, despite playing 90 minutes in Chelsea’s final match, much to the annoyance of the German, who said he “misses too many opportunities to impress”.

The 24-year-old then featured in all four of his club’s Premier League matches ahead of this camp, but was overlooked by Tuchel, who handed maiden call-ups to Jobe Bellingham and Josh King.

“I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception,” Tuchel said.

“We’re speaking now about the player who is not in camp, and it counts when you are in camp.

“And I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp. It was two and a half weeks, and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary and that’s why the credit goes to them.

“The trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

“So it’s not personal, and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country. But the competition is on, and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.

“The door is always open, but nothing has changed, and we decided to do this camp without him.”

Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Aberdeen suffer major double blow as Stephen Robinson confirms injury lay-offs

Palmer was one of five withdrawals ahead of the last camp, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford also pulling out.

Rice is the only one of that quintet recalled as Tuchel reiterated that he will always give preference to those who “walk the talk”.

“The best reactions to the withdrawals in the last camp from the players who were in camp was just to put the quality in and make it a successful camp,” Tuchel said.

“That’s the best foundation for the next camp, to have less withdrawals, which is actually happening now.

“So it’s always about the ones who are in camp.

“It’s always the ones who don’t withdraw and who walk the talk and come to camp and show that it matters and put the quality in. And this is always what we will reward.

“That was always the message, very, very early, since we took charge, that it matters if you are in camp and it matters what you do in camp and the last camp was an excellent one, so the trust and the belief is in the players that were there.”

Mainoo was also overlooked, despite returning to Manchester United’s side.

“I think Kobbie had a difficult spell now with his team and his club, and missed a lot, a lot of matches,” Tuchel said.

“And in the meantime, it was Jobe who impressed in the same level of time, and that’s exactly what we want.

“The door is always open for younger ones to overtake or to make their mark.”

#2019. “Where the problems arise” – Vitiello reveals the ‘truth’ that Milan’s derby win exposed

Antonio Vitiello believes that the derby win over Inter offered one very clear lesson regarding AC Milan’s current status.

The mood around Milan has been buoyed by a fourth straight victory against the city rivals, one that was very much needed after the 4-2 loss to Bologna on Wednesday night that featured a second-half collapse.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Three goals in the first half from Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira demonstrated the potential of this team when everyone is healthy. However, the issue has been when Ruben Amorim has not had all his key men out there.

Vitiello published his weekly column for MilanNews and he chose to focus on the major takeaway from the derby, which was the display of the potential of this team, in contrast to the limitations shown a few nights prior against Bologna.

“The tradition continues. AC Milan have dominated recent derbies and confirmed this in their recent 3-1 victory over the Nerazzurri, demonstrating their much better management of the Milanese derby,” he began.

“The atmosphere is galvanised by the victory, and the San Siro match revealed an unquestionable verdict. When Milan field their first team, it’s a completely different story. The Rossoneri with their best players are truly fearsome.

“When Moreira, Rabiot, Modric, Pulisic, Maignan, and company play together, the other teams have to worry. However, this isn’t always possible due to a tight schedule that forces coaches to change line-ups when there are games every three days.

“It’s literally impossible to consistently field the same team, also to avoid injuries. But that’s where the problems arise. In the long run, the teams with deeper squads, those who don’t suffer too many fluctuations when switching from starters to second string players, prevail. And the derby reaffirmed this truth.

“So, to be truly competitive, the team must improve in the next two transfer windows. First in January, with at least a couple of valuable additions, even spending significant sums. And then next summer, with the second batch of strong players. The next moves are already planned.

“Milan will soon announce their new manager, Markus Krosche, who will oversee the transfer market and in January will focus on a central defender, while also evaluating a winger and a striker. Three players to raise the bar after the summer transfer window ended with some shortcomings. An incomplete transfer window to compete on three fronts simultaneously.

“But this time Gerry Cardinale has chosen to take a risk. He said so himself in a recent interview with ClassCNBC. ‘The decision to finish in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League. Looking at how things had gone over the last four years, I realized it was time for a real change,’ said Gerry Cardinale.

“Compared to previous years, when the club prioritized a profitable budget, this time the decision was to finish in the red. The summer expenses, and those expected in the January transfer window, will lead the club to invest in players to strengthen the squad.

#2015. Mainz 05 vs Bayern Munich - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 05 Nov 2026 22:48

Bayern Munich will hope to maintain their place at the top of the Bundesliga by beating hosts Mainz 05 on Saturday at Mewa Arena.

The Bavarians' tally of 18 points is the same as second-placed Borussia Dortmund, whose inferior goal difference keeps them behind heading into matchweek nine, whereas Mainz are ninth with 10 points.

Mainz's form has been dire, with the club losing four of their last five games in all competitions, including three of their past four league matches.

Manager Urs Fischer will be alarmed by the nature of his team's 4-1 defeat against Elversberg on October 30 given the victors led 3-0 by the interval and led 4-0 by the time they conceded in second-half stoppage time.

The club may be in ninth place, but only three points separate them from 16th-placed Union Berlin, who occupy the division's relegation playoff spot.

Matters will not get any easy for the hosts, who have to face the current top four in their next seven Bundesliga fixtures.

Die Nullfunfer are yet to win at home this season, with Mainz having taken one point from a possible 12 at Mewa Arena, and a loss on the weekend would be their fourth consecutive defeat at the stadium.

Bayern's clash is taking place at exactly the same time as Dortmund's with Elversberg, though they could have entered the weekend ahead of their title rivals on points had they beaten them at Allianz Arena on October 31.

The leaders were held to a 2-2 stalemate by BVB despite twice going ahead, but they conceded an 89th-minute equaliser to draw for the second time in four league games.

Vincent Kompany's side have now drawn four of their past eight matches in all competitions, a period in which they remained unbeaten, while they managed to win 2-0 against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

That clash was the Bavarians' eighth game of the campaign played on the road, and it was their fifth triumph in that time.

The club scored at least two goals in all but one of those matches, but it was also just their second clean sheet away from home this term.

Bayern's record against their hosts is predictably strong, with the visitors having won five of their past seven meetings with Mainz, only losing on one occasion.

Mainz will hope that centre-backs Danny da Costa, Fabio Gruber and Kacper Potulski are at their best, especially as they cannot call upon Dominik Kohr or Stefan Posch, the latter of whom is suspended after being sent off against Elversberg.

Using fewer than three midfielders in midfield could give far too much space to Bayern, so expect to see Jae-Sung Lee, Kaishu Sano and Nadiem Amiri start together on the weekend.

Bayern still have several key injuries in their squad, with forwards Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Serge Gnabry (hamstring) ruled out, while Jamal Musiala (hamstring) is a doubt.

There is no doubt about the selection of Harry Kane, who will be keen to celebrate his new contract with his fifth Bundesliga goal of the season, and he could be supported by an attacking cast of Michael Olise, Lennart Karl and Alphonso Davies.

Joshua Kimmich and Aleksandar Pavlovic are set to patrol the middle of the pitch ahead of centre-backs Dayot Upamecano and Kim Min-Jae.

As for the manager himself, Kompany is still taking an enforced break away from football following his collapse earlier in October that required a hospital visit, meaning assistant Rene Maric will lead the team once again.

Zentner; Da Costa, Gruber, Potulski; Caci, Lee, Sano, Amiri, Widmer; Tietz, Becker

Neuer; Laimer, Upamecano, Kim, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Olise, Karl, Davies; Kane

Bayern may have several injury issues to contend with, but Mainz have struggled considerably in recent weeks.

The visitors could enjoy a fruitful afternoon at Mewa Arena, and striker Kane will relish to opportunity to add to his tally.

#2014. Heartwarming moment Luis Suarez spots former Liverpool team-mate's son - now Chelsea academy starlet - and poses for a photo

Published: 08:34 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 10:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Luis Suarez shared a heartwarming moment with former Liverpool team-mate Glen Johnson's son Kobi while at Inter Miami's training complex in Fort Lauderdale.

The 39-year-old Uruguayan was at the ground for the Messi Cup, a youth tournament the MLS side is hosting, and spotted Kobi Johnson lining up with the rest of the Chelsea Under-14s, who are competing in the United States.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona striker went over to the youngster and said: 'I used to play with your dad, I've known you since you were little.'

The one-time Champions League winner then smiled for a photograph with the youngster.

When asked about the chance encounter, teenage Johnson said: 'He (Suarez) just said like, he remembers when I was a little boy and I was quite chubby, and then he asked for a photo.'

Johnson has been at Chelsea from the under-eights and has risen through the ranks, steadily gaining a reputation as an exciting young talent.

Suarez shared a sweet moment with Glen Johnson's son Kobi at Inter Miami's training ground in the US

Kobi Johnson is currently on the books at Chelsea where he is tipped to follow his father into professional football

Suarez and Johnson spent four seasons together at Liverpool between 2011 and 2015

And it is clear to see where he gets it from, with his father Glen having played 357 Premier League games at Chelsea, Liverpool, Portsmouth and Stoke, even winning the league with Chelsea in 2005 and 2006.

It was at Liverpool, however, where the right-back played with Suarez for four seasons between 2011 and 2015 - with the pair were part of a memorable Liverpool team that narrowly missed out on the title back in 2014 after the famous 'Gerrard slip' at Stamford Bridge.

It was during that period too that Suarez was accused of racially abusing former Manchester United left-back Patrice Evra during a Premier League grudge match between the two clubs in 2011.

Suarez was subsequently banned for eight matches after it was ruled that he had used racist language towards Evra.

Johnson controversially publicly defended him at the time, and years later, continued to be conflicted over the incident.

Speaking on talkSPORT in 2019, Johnson said: 'Carra (former team-mate Jamie Carragher) was right to apologise and I'd have to agree with him; I think the timing of it was wrong as the ban was so close.

'But in the club's defence, they were just trying to support one of their players.

'I don't think anyone in that dressing room or at the club believed Luis was racist or capable of being racist.'

While 42-year-old Johnson is enjoying his retirement after leaving the professional game for good in 2018, Suarez is still plying his trade in America at Inter Miami alongside other Barcelona legends like Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi.

#2011. Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team

Neil McCann will continue his drive to see Kilmarnock “flourish” in the face of growing fan scrutiny.

The Ayrshire club are one point ahead of William Hill Premiership bottom side Hibernian, with nine points from 36 and having conceded 28 goals from 12 games amid concern and disgruntlement among a section of the Killie support.

McCann is preparing his players to take on a Celtic team who are four points ahead of Rangers at the top of the table, having played a game more and on the back of a morale-boosting 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas on Thursday night

However, the Kilmarnock boss remains positive, and said: “Supporters will always give their opinion when they come into the stadium and they’ll voice it. They’re entitled to voice their opinion.

“My pressure, to be honest with you, is preparing our players tactically, physically, mentally.

Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

“And then when they take the field, I give them full autonomy to go and carry out all of those instructions, but play with the freedom and bravery that got us out of trouble last year.

“Nothing’s changed in my build-up. Nothing’s changed in my drive. Nothing’s changed in my approach to getting Kilmarnock to be a team that wants to put on a product on the pitch.

“A lot’s been made of ‘you can just win games and it’s all about winning games’. And I absolutely get that when it comes to management.

“Of course, it’s about results, very much, it’s a results-driven business. But I was given this job to get us out of bother last year.

“And we came in, the first thing wasn’t about, yes, results were important, but it was making sure that the team were capable and prepared to go and get those results.

“I think we are prepared to go and get those results. We just haven’t given our support enough good days to celebrate wins.

“But the work doesn’t stop. And it doesn’t deter me one bit from the work that I do on the training field.

“I’ll hopefully see a team flourish, get the results that I think their performances deserve. And then we can all come together with the unity that we showed last season and hopefully Kilmarnock will start climbing the table.”

#2007. Sky Germany: Krösche heading for Milan but compensation must be discussed – the situation

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Now, Sky Germany confirm that Krösche’s future likely lies in Italy because a move to Milan is becoming increasingly likely. However, no deal has been finalised yet: officials from both clubs still need to hold talks as Krösche is only on leave from Frankfurt.

His contract, which runs until 2028, is currently still valid. The 46-year-old insisted on having a release clause included in his contract. Specifically, this means that any club wanting to hire him before the summer of 2027 will have to pay a fee of approximately €5-7m, or negotiate with Eintracht.

No advanced talks have yet taken place, but Sky do add that Krösche is expected to take on the role of Head of Football with Milan. A start date of January 1, 2027 – coinciding with the start of the winter transfer window – is being discussed.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

#2005. Huddersfield Town vs Exeter City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:51

Aiming to continue an eight-match winning streak, Huddersfield Town will welcome Exeter City to the Accu Stadium on Saturday for an FA Cup first-round tie.

The hosts have climbed to the top of the League One with a hot streak, while their visitors saw an unbeaten run of their own come to an end last weekend and sit 12th in League Two.

Huddersfield Town will kick off their 2026-27 FA Cup bid at the weekend on the back of a strong run in League One.

The Terriers have failed to get past this stage in the previous two years, most recently losing to Bolton Wanderers last time around, but they do come in with plenty of confidence, currently sitting top of League One in their first full season under Martin Drury after falling short of the playoffs in their first two terms in the third tier.

In 14 league games since Drury was handed the reins permanently over the summer, the Yorkshire outfit have managed 29 points, winning eight and only losing one of those matches while scoring a league-high tally of 28 goals.

That solitary defeat came in mid-September, and the Terriers have since won six of eight games in all competitions and five in seven league outings while drawing the other two, most recently hosting fellow promotion-chasers Luton Town on the back of four straight triumphs in midweek and drawing 1-1 with thanks to Joe Taylor's second-half hat-trick.

Now turning their focus to the FA Cup, Huddersfield Town will hope to channel their league form into Saturday's first-round tie and continue their hot streak with another victory.

Their opponents, meanwhile, face a tough test in the first round having reached the fourth and third rounds in their prior two campaigns.

Exeter City enter this year's competition on the back of a mixed start to life back in League Two after relegation last term, having struggled to get up and running early on.

Matt Taylor's team earned just six points from their first eight games in England's fourth tier but reversed their fortunes in a near-perfect October, winning four and drawing one in a five-match run culminating in victories over Crewe Alexandra and Fleetwood Town to climb into the top half.

That run also came alongside an EFL Trophy tie against third-tier Oxford United, in which the Grecians drew and won the penalty shootout, but their unbeaten run came to an end at the weekend, visiting leaders Salford City and losing 2-1 having led through Sonny Cox and conceded second-half goals to Luke Garbutt and Will Aimson.

Still with plenty of optimism to take from their much-improved run in October, Exeter City will now bid to pull off an upset in Yorkshire to progress to the FA Cup second round.

Huddersfield Town form (all competitions):

After a busy and successful run in League One, Drury may opt to rotate his Huddersfield team at the weekend to rest some key men and afford opportunities for squad players, although Jack Whatmough, Herbie Kane, Marcus McGuane, Murray Wallace and Bojan Radulovic will likely remain sidelined by injuries.

Joe Taylor and summer signing Derensili Sanches Fernandes have both been pivotal in attack, with the former on 10 goals in 13 league appearances this term and the latter racking up seven goals and six assists in 14 league matches since his summer arrival, and they may both be handed a well-earned rest with Ashley Fletcher and Samson Tovide likely to come in.

The injuries leave the Terriers light in midfield, but David Kasumu can come in to relieve either Archie Collins or Cameron Humphreys, while Joe Low should return to the defence from the outset.

Exeter City are contending with a long injury list, as Jake Doyle-Hayes, Gwion Edwards, Ajay Matthews, Danny Rose and Daniel Watts sidelined.

Goals have been spread out across the squad this season with no one on more than two but six players tied on that number, including Cox who should again lead the attack after his opener against Salford.

Reece Cole may come in to support him alongside Anthony Scully and Taylor Perry, while Charlie Cummins a mainstay at the base of the midfield.

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:

Young; Low, Bowat, Roughan; Bronkhorst, Humphreys, Kasumu, Gooch; Ashia; Tovide, Fletcher

Bycroft; Samuel, Taylor, Fitzwater, Woodhouse; Kite, Cummins; Cole, Perry, Scully; Cox

Huddersfield Town are far more likely than their visitors to shuffle the pack on Saturday, but the Terriers have momentum and strength in depth, even despite their injuries, and should have more than enough to continue their strong run of form with squad players keen to impress.

#2000. Ex-Celtic star tells Martin O'Neill why he's on receiving end of 'flak with love'

Joe Hart has told Martin O'Neill why he is getting "flak with love" amid Celtic's stuttering form.

Scrutiny at the club is growing and growing after a draw with Dundee United was followed up by defeat to Falkirk. Previously, the domestic form had been almost flawless, but for losing to Rangers.

Fans are now concerned their lead at the top of the table is precarious and are questioning the direction of the club even more.

Former Parkhead goalkeeper Hart says that scrutiny is always going to be there and it does not affect O'Neill's standing with the support.

He told The Overlap: "It’s flak with love, and that doesn’t make any sense. Of course, we know it doesn’t make any sense, but Martin O’Neill will be, and is, absolutely adored. But he knows what he signed up for as a Celtic manager, and he would expect to be getting a lot of questions asked about him.

Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

And that’s not saying he’s not up to the task or he’s not the man for the job, but that’s what comes with the territory. If you really understand Celtic, you understand that if you’re not borderline perfect domestically and challenging in Europe, you’re going to get it.

"You’re going to get it because they care and they’re intelligent football fans. And, there’s a massive disharmony with the board. The fans really don’t understand what the direction of the club is. And obviously the board have got their opinions in terms of the success that they had and continue to have.

So, it is difficult. That was really shining brightly mid-season last season, but then Martin came back in and the team started to win and it goes away. It’s amazing what winning can do, and at the moment they’re not.

"They had a difficult result at Falkirk. I think they drew at home to Dundee United. And then this Besiktas game felt ominous. It felt like there was going to be a riot, or not even a riot. Do you know what the worst feeling you can have in a stadium is? And I very rarely felt it up there. It wasn’t anger, it was people going, ‘Pfft, we lost again.’ That is the worst feeling you could have.

"You’d rather have someone that impassioned, that embroiled as a Celtic fan. Like I say, domestically, I lost very, very few games, but no matter what run you’d been on, you could feel it. It wasn’t the majority, but you’d feel some people’s whole life and whole livelihood is proudly Celtic.

"And if you don’t perform in that shirt, you’re going to get it. I’ve still got friends up there, and they were flat going into the game. If Celtic had lost, they wouldn’t have been angry, they’d have been like, ‘Oh, God.’ And that’s not a nice feeling. I talked about it for Michael [Carrick], but I think it’s a little bit different up there, because they’re still top of the league.

"If they can take the atmosphere that they generated towards the end of the game last night into the league game this weekend, I think it’s Kilmarnock, then it could be a massive spark to go again.”

#1994. Stuttgart vs Werder Bremen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 05 Nov 2026 23:00, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:25

Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga comes from the MHPArena as Stuttgart welcome a high-flying Werder Bremen side.

While the hosts look to bounce back from a disappointing Champions League defeat, the visitors will have their sights set on extending their unbeaten league run to eight games.

Stuttgart’s inconsistent start to the season continued on Tuesday night when Sebastian Hoeness and his men suffered a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Galatasaray.

That was the third defeat in six games for the Swabians, who also tripped up against Hamburger SV and Borussia Monchengladbach - results which leave them 11th in the Bundesliga table, with nine points from eight matches.

The majority of Stuttgart’s recent fixtures have come on the road, but their home form has offered little encouragement either, with the club failing to record a victory on their own turf since early September.

In reality, Stuttgart were never in the title conversation at the start of the season, though mounting successes over recent seasons have certainly lifted expectations.

However, with the Swabians sitting just two points above the relegation zone and nine adrift of the top two, pressure is beginning to mount on Hoeness and his players.

Trouble is, Stuttgart have only managed one win from five previous meetings with Werder Bremen. That sole success came last season, when the Swabians swept their rivals aside in a 4-0 romping.

Unbeaten in seven Bundesliga games and chasing a third successive league victory, Werder Bremen are undoubtedly the form team heading into Saturday's encounter.

Last weekend, Bremen comfortably dispatched Hoffenheim with a 2-0 victory, having beaten Mainz 05 a fortnight earlier thanks to a Niclas Fullkrug double.

Speaking of the current Bundesliga top scorer, the former West Ham man will be hoping to continue his momentum - especially when he goes head-to-head against his national team rival, Deniz Undav.

That adds an intriguing subplot to Saturday's contest, with Fullkrug potentially looking to prove Jurgen Klopp right after the national team coach selected the Bremen striker but left Undav out of his latest squad.

Another interesting angle concerns Bremen's away form, which has been considerably less impressive than their recent performances on home soil.

Daniel Thioune’s side have only managed two wins from six games on the road, and one of those was a DFB-Pokal victory over fifth-tier side Luneburger Hansa.

More concerning, though, is their defensive record on the road, having conceded 12 goals across their five away league trips.

Atakan Karazor is the big doubt for Stuttgart ahead of the weekend, with the midfielder struggling with a thigh injury.

According to Hoeness, a recent MRI scan revealed visible bleeding, meaning the 30-year-old is highly unlikely to start Saturday’s game.

Angelo Stiller, Karazor's usual midfield partner, has also been ruled out until the international break with an adductor problem, leaving the Swabians short of options in the middle of the park.

Justin Diehl (thigh), Leo Sauer (muscle), Josha Vagnoman (hamstring) and Dan-Axel Zagadou (hamstring) are also out of action.

As for Werder Bremen, the visitors will make the trip to Stuttgart without nine first-team players.

Experienced midfielder Mitchell Weiser became the latest addition to the injury list after picking up a hamstring problem against Hoffenheim.

Third-choice goalkeeper Markus Kolke was never in contention for a starting place on Saturday, though a training injury this week has left him unavailable anyway.

Felix Agu (muscle), Skelly Alvero (calf), Paul Erevbenagie (ankle), Salim Musah (hamstring), Moussa N'Diaye (groin), Jens Stage (thigh) and Keke Topp (knee) are all on the sidelines.

In more positive news, Niklas Stark could make his return after his name did not appear on the list of unavailable players during Thioune’s recent press conference.

#1993. Eyupspor vs Kocaelispor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 05 Nov 2026 23:09

Eyupspor will be looking to end their miserable run of league defeats when they welcome Kocaelispor to Esenyurt Necmi Kadioglu Stadium on Saturday in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts have lost seven consecutive league matches and sit bottom of the standings with just three points from their opening 10 fixtures, while the visitors occupy eighth place with 16 points after collecting five victories this season.

Eyupspor have endured a disastrous start to the campaign, losing nine of their 10 matches, with their latest league setback coming in a humiliating 5-1 defeat away to Amed SK.

However, Mustafa Dalci's side did secure a morale-boosting Turkish Cup victory in midweek, recording a 4-2 win away to lower-division side Fethiyespor on Wednesday.

The four goals they scored in that match were more than they have managed in the league all season, having found the net just three times, the lowest tally in the division, while their defensive problems are equally evident, with 28 goals conceded, the worst record in the competition.

Dalci has struggled to make an impact since replacing Ozhan Pulat earlier in the campaign, with the Turkish manager yet to record a league victory, while his team have scored just once and conceded 12 goals in the league under his leadership.

Their home performances have offered little encouragement either, having lost four of their five league matches at Esenyurt Necmi Kadioglu Stadium, although their only victory did come on home soil against Genclerbirligi.

Kocaelispor, meanwhile, have enjoyed a considerably better campaign and head into this fixture comfortably placed in the top half of the standings, having gone unbeaten in their last three matches across all competitions.

The visitors were held to a goalless draw by Caykur Rizespor in their most recent league outing, having previously beaten Mazidagi 3-0 in the Turkish Cup and Alanyaspor 2-1 in the league.

Selcuk Inan's side will be hoping to secure consecutive away victories for the first time since earning promotion to the top flight last season, and they will be confident of their chances given the struggles of their hosts.

Their away record is not flawless, having lost three of their five league trips, but two victories on the road suggest they have enough quality to take advantage of Eyupspor's defensive vulnerabilities.

The head-to-head record also favours the visitors, who have won their last three meetings with Eyupspor, including a 1-0 victory at Esenyurt Necmi Kadioglu Stadium in March 2026.

Eyupspor have one reported injury concern ahead of Saturday's encounter, with Talha Ulvan doubtful after picking up a muscle problem.

Yalcin Barasi is expected to retain his place as the central striker, with Leandro Pintor and Bilal Boutobba likely to provide support from the wider positions.

Kocaelispor, meanwhile, have more significant availability concerns, with Tanguy Zoukrou, Massadio Haidara and Bruno Petkovic all expected to miss out through injury.

Berkan Kutlu will be an important figure for the visitors after scoring four league goals this season, while Florian Aye and Goncalo Sousa should provide further attacking options.

#1992. Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to

Mika Baur is enjoying the demands of being a Celtic player – and was delighted to see the team display their fighting spirit and belief as they broke their Europa League duck.

The 22-year-old impressed as Celtic came from behind to beat Besiktas 3-2 on Thursday and get off the mark in the Europa League at the fourth time of asking.

The Hoops were heading for a seventh defeat in 11 matches when they fell behind early in the second half but the introduction of Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Colby Donovan on the hour mark sparked the team into life.

Manager Martin O’Neill recently admitted that some new players were still adapting to the demands of playing for Celtic but Baur and Duran have quickly proved they were successful summer signings.

Baur arrived from Paderborn after helping them to promotion to the Bundesliga and made his Germany debut last month, but moving to Scotland has been a new experience.

Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

“To play every three days is different for me,” the midfielder said. “I think I have played the same amount of games now that I had last season by the winter break.

“But I like it. That’s what you want. You want to play all the time, more playing than training. I am really enjoying it.

“And I think the pressure to win is a good kind of pressure. It’s better than (trying) not to lose. So I really enjoy it.”

Baur has shown pace and skill on the ball but his pressing in the final stages drew massive appreciation from the crowd on Thursday.

“First of all, I want to work hard for the team, for myself, that I can prove myself and I can play on the stage, help the team, put in a shift, hard work,” he said.

“That’s what I have to do first. And then after this, the skill comes, playing with the ball. But first of all, it’s showing heart on the field. I was really happy that it was appreciated.”

The win over the Turkish side felt like it could be a major step in Celtic’s season as they bounced back from losing the opening goal and from a late equaliser, with Duran netting the winner seconds later.

“The second half was pure heart, pure fight,” Baur said. “I’m not here for a long time, but I think that’s what it’s all about. This win feels unbelievable because we deserved it. We fought for it.

“The team is really, really close together. We know that we had a tough couple of weeks, but you can feel it in the training sessions, how the team is working together, the feeling, the believing is always there. And it was there on the pitch. That’s what we have to show week by week, every three days.

“It was not just our win. The atmosphere was great. I’m really, really thankful for every supporter in the stadium. They gave us a lot of energy. We all fight together. That makes me happy.”

#1991. Kaka speaks for the first time since San Siro tears: “Milan is second home to me”

One of the most striking images from AC Milan’s derby win over Inter on Saturday was Ricardo Kaka’s tears as he was welcomed on the field.

Saturday night was the night of Milan’s resounding derby victory – their fourth in a row against Inter – but it was also the night of Kakà’s return to San Siro. He was presented with a trophy before kick-off to mark his induction into the Rossoneri Hall of Fame.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a moment filled with emotion for all the fans present who chanted his name, but above all it was a moving moment for Kakà himself, who couldn’t hold back the tears as a montage video played on the screen.

Now, the Brazilian has spoken for the first time since that memorable evening as the NSS Sports Instagram page published a short interview with him.

“Milan is a second home to me: that’s the word that comes to mind when I think of this city. I’ve been truly fortunate to have so many great champions at my side, at AC Milan, in the national team, in Madrid: I’ve played with some truly brilliant players.

“The most elegant? Zidane, even though I didn’t play with him, but against him. The best moments associated with San Siro are definitely the victories, the Champions League celebrations in 2007, so many matches like the one against Manchester United or the one against Roma when we won the Scudetto.

“But there were also many moments, every time I entered San Siro and heard the chant ‘Siam venuti fin qua, siam venuti fin qua…’, I got goosebumps.”
