#1915. GdS: Milan to sign record-breaking €500m deal with Adidas – the details

There has been talk about AC Milan moving to Adidas in recent weeks and that has now gone a step further, with details of the deal filtering.

By all accounts, next year will see Milan end their partnership with Puma. The two have worked together since 2018 – when the Rossoneri stopped working with the iconic German brand – and produced several kits in that time.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, with a focus on improving commercial value, Gerry Cardinale has now looked to the kit and decided to head back to what some may call home.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Diavolo will sign a blockbuster deal with the three-stripe brand, worth €500 million across 10 seasons. In other words, they’ll earn a record-breaking €50m per season, as opposed to the reported €30m.

A deal with potential for ‘exponential growth’, it’s a €36m increase on the current contract with Puma – worth €14m per season – and significantly changes the value of the shirt. Looking elsewhere, Juventus’ deal with Adidas is believed to be worth €408m across 10 seasons, whilst Inter’s eight-year deal was worth €30m per season.

Above all, though, it’s a romantic return and a symbol of hope to return to better times. Throughout the history of their partnership, Milan have often been at the top, and it’s one of the most recognisable relationships in Italian (and European) football. Now, it’s coming back.

#1914. Bukayo Saka ‘a bit fragile,’ reckons former Arsenal and Manchester United defender

Bukayo Saka is ‘a bit fragile’ and must work on preventing injury problems in future, reckons former Arsenal defender Mikael Silvestre.

The Gunners winger is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem picked up in a Champions League clash with Bayern Munich on October 21.

Saka is not expected to be back in action until December, with Noni Madueke filling in on the right flank in his absence.

The 25-year-old has been hampered by some injury issues over the last two seasons, but has still managed to rack up a huge amount of appearances, 323 for Arsenal in total.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He played 49 times in all competitions last season, although the 2024/25 campaign saw him play the least since he broke into the first team, turning out 37 times.

Silvestre accepts that injuries are bound to occur for players of Saka’s ilk, but suggests he is not quite as robust as he could be.

‘When you are an explosive player like Saka, obviously the muscles are what will trouble you when you are doing those sprints all the time,’ Silvestre told PariuriX.com. ‘Maybe, he is a bit fragile, and with the amount of games things like this can happen.

‘What is important for him is the recovery and the prevention, because it’s very important for him that it doesn’t happen too often, because he is very important for Arsenal.’

Silvestre sees Madueke as an improving force in Saka’s absence, although there is still room to become sharper in the final third.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘That’s why you have a big squad and Madueke would start for most of the teams in the Premier League, if not all,’ said the Frenchman. ‘He has the quality and I think he is getting his confidence now, he is trying to score and create more.

‘He doesn’t have the killer instinct yet, but he is growing into it and he is trying to get there.’

Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with Manchester United, reckons Arsenal’s forward line as a whole can let them down, with their strength clearly lying in defence. The recent 1-0 win at Liverpool being a good illustration.

‘Winning at Anfield, with a clean sheet as well makes it a very good defensive performance,’ he said. ‘We can’t say the same with the offense. I would say that’s one for the record, and one that you look back at the end of the season and say it was an important 3 points. But it wasn’t a full on, top class, 90 minute performance from Arsenal.

‘But it’s important to get those wins against teams who are also potentially in the race, and to keep your distance from them.

‘The positives are the defensive side of things, the 3 points, and the fact that it was at Anfield. It breaks that negative dynamic but I think it’s just for the stats really.

‘I think you need your best players at the key moments featuring in the semi-finals and the final of competitions. Arsenal need to keep Timber fit, Saliba is coming back also. You need your strong 11 and the best defence once you reach the final. So it’s still a long way away but they defend well, as a unit for sure.’

#1913. JEFF POWELL MBE: I witnessed the unstoppable rot that caused Man United's last relegation - now the ghosts are resurfacing in alarmingly similar fashion for Michael Carrick and his rag-bag of players

By JEFF POWELL MBE, SPORTS WRITER AND BOXING COLUMNIST

Published: 12:02 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EDT, 2 November 2026

What more spooky time of the year for a fog of deja vu to be hanging over the haunted house of Old Trafford.

The ghosts of Halloween half a century past have materialised to foretell the doom of relegation.

The omens of 1974 are rewritten in the statistics cursing the current Manchester United team. No win in the first seven away games. A manager without a victory in nine consecutive matches. Perhaps coming up next, a run of only four wins in 20 league matches to match that of the relegation season 52 years ago.

And so to Gloomy Tuesday. If United fail to defeat Roma in the Champions League, they will equal their worst sequence of results in 75 years. The ominous portent for this one is much more recent. If they could lose 4-1 to lowly Como the other week, what chance of beating a major Italian club, unbeaten so far this season in Serie A? With this rag-bag of players, not much.

United’s class of ’74 included England’s Alex Stepney, David Sadler and Brian Kidd, Scotland stars Martin Buchan, George Graham, Lou Macari, Jim McCalliog and Willie Morgan. Graham recalls: ‘The club was going through a difficult time but we did our best.’

Of the team which self-destructed in defeat at Chelsea this Saturday, that could only be truly said of one man. Harry Maguire has survived more criticism than he ever deserved and once again he was alone in looking like he objected to losing.

Denis Law (second right), then of Manchester City, condemns his old club United to relegation in 1974

Following the 2-0 loss at Chelsea on Saturday, if United fail to defeat Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday they will equal their worst sequence of results in 75 years

One of his team-mates, the typically disgraceful Argentine Lisandro Martinez, made sure of defeat by getting himself sent off. Whether that act was deliberate only he can tell us but he looked as anxious to depart this great though ailing club as he had sounded when he criticised its executives after the Como loss.

As did the so-called captain. I voted for Bruno Fernandes as the Footballer of Last Year. Never again. By adding his voice to that of Martinez, he cheapened this great club in its hour of need. That he tried to recant relegates him to the same league of hypocritical back-trackers as Andy Burnham.

The damage to an already badly wounded Michael Carrick has been done. It became irreparable when he agreed to make the peace.

Sir Alex Ferguson would never have forgiven such a breach of trust. But then we are comparing pears with apples here. Fergie is a genius. Carrick simply an honest man out of his depth.

The unfavourable comparisons with the relegation of yesteryear don’t end there. Fernandes is a talented footballer but the idol of ‘74 was another genius.

George Best electrified not only Old Trafford but the world of football and beyond. Champions League glory, two English league titles, Wembley Cup finals, heroic if inevitably hopeless World Cup brilliance with Northern Ireland and a Ballon d’Or would have only been for starters had he not succumbed to his lust for booze and blondes which not only terminated his career but shortened his star-spangled but ultimately tragic life.

Bruno may become remembered as a footnote to Eusebio and Ronaldo in Portugal’s hall of fame. Besty will shine forever in the pantheon of football’s all-time greats.

Best knew when it was the right, self-destructed time to leave. Having torn himself away from Old Trafford in the summer of ’73 he allowed himself to be talked back by the retired Busby.

George Best (left) knew when it was the right time to leave. Having torn himself away from Old Trafford in 1973 he allowed himself to be talked back by the retired Matt Busby (right)

The damage to an already badly wounded Michael Carrick has been done. It became irreparable when he agreed to make peace with the players who spoke out against the club

After a dozen games he accepted that his best would no longer be electrifying enough to spark salvation and after an away defeat on New Year’s Day he said his last goodbye.

As sharp between the ears, surprisingly to some, as he was undeniably mesmerising on the pitch, he left behind words of wisdom gleaned from watching as boy and man as United fell into the turmoil of finding a manager to succeed Sir Matt.

They are as relevant in this time of crisis as they were those 52 years ago: ‘The fear of relegation starts in the boardroom, comes down to the managers and through to the players. The fans sense it.’

The faithful are, indeed, well aware of the origin of the rot besetting the Reds today. They detest the Glazers who brought their American opportunism and apparent greed to Manchester and have plunged the club into billions of debt. They are disenchanted already with Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Not least because this penny-pinching Englishman’s cost-cutting has broken the hearts of so many loyal servants by sacking them from jobs they loved as much as they do their team. No matter how badly it is playing just now. And, by the way, he can stick his big-top circus stadium in the proverbial orifice.

Manchester United, like Liverpool, belong to the people. Not some damn Yankees and an English fat cat.

Unless this one reclaims its heart, soul, very reason for existing – and damn quickly – the ruin may take decades to rebuild. If ever.

United were heading this way when they were running mindlessly through managers in the 70s and 80s – Dave Sexton was sacked after finishing second in the league for heaven’s sake – until they got lucky as Sir Matt came briefly out of retirement to find his own successor in Sir Alex.

Manchester United, like Liverpool, belong to the people. Not some damn Yankees and an English fat cat in Jim Ratcliffe (centre)

Alex Ferguson (centre, flanked by director Mike Edelson and chairman Martin Edwards) at his unveiling as United boss in 1986, thanks to the help of Busby

The next Greatest Of All Time may never be out there. Carrick accepts it’s not him but the sympathies of the Red Army for a good man doing his darndest for a club he loves as much as they do may keep him going long enough for the increasingly fearful men in the boardroom to make a proper, lasting appointment rather than yet another shot in the dark.

For this they need to take sensible advice from more experienced football men. Just as they must set aside their misguided belief that they know something about the game itself and let seasoned judges guide them towards the really, really best players in which to invest their millions.

Rather than the rabble among the present first team of whose names neither they, nor more importantly the Stretford End, had ever heard until they ambled into Old Trafford.

As the money men should know, if you buy cheap you end up having to buy again. If they don’t, they should follow senors Martinez and Fernandes out of the building.

#1912. 'We’ve been a shadow' - Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones' admission ahead of Sheffield United test

Nathan Jones has conceded his Charlton Athletic side have been “a shadow” ahead of their clash with Sheffield United tomorrow (November 7).

Chris Wilder’s Blades appear to have turned a corner in the Championship, while Jones’ Addicks are reeling after four straight league defeats.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

They were beaten by Bolton Wanderers earlier this week having previously been seen off by Middlesbrough, Norwich City and Watford.

“It’s always about us,” said Jones. “Yes, we have to nullify opposition threats but it’s always about us and that’s the thing that we can affect.

“That’s what we haven’t been [doing]. We’ve been a shadow of us over these last three or four games.

“I get paid to do this. This is what I get paid to do Part of that, as the manager, is leading a group and getting the best out of a group. I get applauded when we do well and overachieve, and the buck falls with me when we’re not. So I’m really looking forward to the challenge.

“If my players are as ready as I am, then we’ll be difficult to beat. Some of the performances have been there, but we’ve not been us on a regular basis. If we are us, we can compete.”

Sheffield United will be looking to capitalise upon Charlton’s error-prone nature, as Jones’ men have developed a nasty habit of gifting goals away.

“First and foremost, you’ve got to put in a full performance,” said Jones. “A full performance means that you don’t make big errors and you don’t gift goals.

“You make people work, and then you can rely on your structure and the work that you do to shut out the opposition.

“When you do the work in possession and all the attacking work, then you just want that to be executed on the day and help us to score goals. We’ve not been doing that enough. When we’ve scored, we’ve not defended. When we’ve made mistakes, we have been punished. But that’s our fault for making mistakes.”

#1911. ‘Ridiculous threat’ – Xabi Alonso told that ex-Liverpool star would ‘thrive’ at Chelsea

Alan Hutton believes that Trent Alexander-Arnold would ‘thrive’ if he reunited with former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

Alexander-Arnold left his boyhood club Liverpool to join the Spanish giants two summers ago, but injuries saw him feature just 21 times in the league under Alonso and his interim replacement, Alvaro Arbeloa.

While fit this campaign, the Englishman has still struggled for regular minutes under Jose Mourinho and has started just one of Real’s last six matches in all competitions.

Summer signing Denzel Dumfries has moved above Alexander-Arnold in the pecking order, while Mourinho has also deployed Federico Valverde as a makeshift right-back over the Englishman.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Given that lack of game time, Hutton believes that Alexander-Arnold may soon start to consider his options.

And the former Premier League full-back earmarked Chelsea as the perfect club to get the 28-year-old back to his best.

‘Trent Alexander-Arnold could thrive at Chelsea because Xabi Alonso would use him in the correct manner and get the best out of him, because his attacking threat is ridiculous,’ Hutton told OLBG.

‘What he sees, his vision, his passing ability, it’s right up there.

‘It is strange when you watch Real Madrid, I was watching El Clásico and Valverde played at right-back while Dumfries and Trent were on the bench.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Even for me, as good a player as Valverde is, he’s a midfielder, so that would hurt you a bit. It’s been a shame that it hasn’t quite worked out, but he’s so talented.

‘I think a move back to the Premier League would suit him, he knows it inside out. Someone like Alonso, with what he’d want from him, would use him in the correct manner and get the best out of him.’

Speaking recently, Mourinho admitted that omitting Alexander-Arnold has been a painful decision.

‘First of all, it hurts me. I don’t like to make players feel bad. I want them to feel good,’ Mourinho said.

‘Obviously, when you build a squad with two players per position as your foundation and then have a third player take the field, that’s something I don’t like.

‘But there are things that are more important than these feelings. Things that are more important for the team at a given moment. And I decided that right now, the move was to change up the midfield and put Fede [Valverde] in there.’

And with speculation likely to mount ahead of the January transfer window, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield.

‘I’d have him back,’ Carragher said on The Overlap. ‘He would get a lot of criticism, because I think he made a mistake. I think he made a big mistake going to Madrid.

‘We’ve definitely missed his creativity.’

#1910. FC Cincinnati vs Nashville SC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 01:11, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:06

FC Cincinnati will look to secure a spot in the first round of the MLS playoffs when they take on Nashville SC at TQL Stadium on Saturday.

Nashville head into MLS Decision Day with their fate already sealed, having clinched their first-ever Supporters' Shield.

Cincinnati are sitting in seventh spot in the Eastern Conference after winning 12, losing 11 and drawing 10 of their 33 matches this season.

Pat Noonan's side have come into form at just the right time, having dropped just two points from their last four matches since suffering consecutive defeats against New England Revolution and Columbus Crew.

Cincinnati recorded home and away wins in back-to-back games against DC United, before they played out a thrilling 2-2 draw against Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Orange and Blue then returned to winning ways with a narrow 1-0 home victory against Philadelphia Union, which came courtesy of Ayoub Jabbari's third goal of the season.

Having already guaranteed some form of post-season action, Cincinnati will secure a spot in the first round with a win against Nashville, but a failure to claim all three points will leave them open to being overtaken by Columbus and Orlando City, who currently occupy the two wild-card round positions.

The hosts can take some confidence from the fact they have won two of their last three MLS home games against Nashville, including a 2-1 success in September 2025 at TQL Stadium.

Nashville will already have one eye on the first round of the playoffs after clinching their first MLS Supporters' Shield with a 2-0 win over Montreal last month.

BJ Callaghan's side went on to play out a goalless draw against Philadelphia Union before coming from two goals down to pull off a 3-2 victory over New York Red Bulls last time out.

Sam Surridge netted a stoppage-time winner in that comeback success, which extended the club's impressive 17-game unbeaten home run in the MLS.

In fact, they have gone nine matches without defeat at any venue since losing away to Toronto FC on September 27, so they will be desperate to carry that undefeated streak into the playoffs as they continue to work towards their ultimate goal of winning the MLS Cup for the first time in their history.

Having tied the MLS single-season points record, Nashville will take the outright record if they are able to add at least a point to their 74-point tally in their final outing of the regular season.

Nashville will certainly fancy their chances of claiming a positive result after running out 4-0 winners in their most recent meeting with Cincinnati at Geodis Park in August.

Cincinnati defender Tyrell Malacia is unlikely to prove his fitness in time, having been forced to sit out the last three matches with an ankle injury.

The hosts are also without the services of Julian Malatini and Miles Robinson, while Teenage Hadebe is hoping to prove his fitness after being withdrawn with an apparent injury issue in the win over Philadelphia.

Evander is in contention to start the final regular season game after featuring as a half-time substitute last weekend.

As for the visitors, they have reported no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday's away trip, which should give Callaghan a full squad to choose from.

The likes of Daniel Lovitz, Edvard Tagseth, Alex Muyl and Warren Madrigal could come into Callaghan's thinking if he wants to manage minutes ahead of the playoffs.

That said, Surridge will surely be keen to retain his place as he looks to add to the 19 goals he has scored in the regular season.

Celentano; Smith, Hagglund, Hadebe; Mboma, Bucha, Nwobodo, Evander, Ramirez; Barlow, Denkey

Schwake; Najar, Palacios, Woledzi, Lovitz; Espinoza, Yazbek, Tagseth, Muyl; Madrigal, Surridge

Nashville carry a nine-game unbeaten run into Saturday's fixture, and while there may be changes to their starting lineup, we think they will do enough to extend their undefeated streak with a draw.

#1909. 'Carnage' - Ex-Wolves goalkeeper Carl Ikeme offers insight into Doncaster Rovers' infamous experiment

Former Doncaster Rovers goalkeeper Carl Ikeme has lifed the lid on his experience of the club’s now-infamous 2011/12 season ‘experiment’.

The now-retired stopper had two loan spells at Doncaster during that ill-fated Championship campaign, building experience away from his parent club Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was dropped into an environment far from ordinary, as Doncaster turned to high-profile figures signed to short-term deals to keep them in the second tier.

Among those recruited with the help of agent Willie McKay were former Liverpool maverick El Hadji Diouf, ex-Newcastle United defender Habib Beye and France-capped frontman Frédéric Piquionne.

“It was a bit chaotic in all honesty,” Ikeme told The Yorkshire Post. “I'm sure a lot of people have said the same.

“We had El Hadji Diouf and Pascal Chimbonda and a few other characters. I think there was talent in the squad, but I think in order to get a few of these players here, Dean Saunders kind of had to let them do what they wanted in a way, which didn't really help Doncaster.

“It was frustrating for a lot of the players that were training all the time. You probably heard some lads would just come on a Friday and train and play Saturday.

“It all seemed okay at the time if you're looking maybe from an outside point of view, but when you're in it yourself, it's a bit of a p**s take.”

Ikeme only dropped in at Doncaster for two short-term loans but committed to relocating to the area from his Midlands home.

“It was frustrating because I was living up there and obviously you had lads who would come down on a Friday,” the now-40-year-old said. “I'm staying up Doncaster all week, which is fine because that's my job.

“But it just gets frustrating I think and you had some good lads there as well, but it was hard work in all honesty.”

The so-called experiment was unequivocally a failure and Doncaster tumbled into League One at the end of the season.

Ikeme was back at Wolves by the time relegation was confirmed and did not leave Molineux again, seeing out his career with the club before retiring in 2018.

“It makes you know what you're not about, and what you don't want,” he said. “But at the same time I met some great people at Doncaster.

“Dave ‘Mud’ Richards, the kitman, great guy. Mal Purchase, who went everywhere with Dean, another great character man, really good guy. The goalkeeper coach, there were a lot of good people there behind the scenes, but it was just carnage and it wasn't how a team should really be run.

“I understand it to a degree, but football is a tough game and sometimes it doesn't really matter if you've got players that are supposed to be above the level, if they don't really care then it's going to be difficult.

“Obviously the Championship's outrageously hard anyway, and if everyone's not pulling in the same direction it becomes really difficult, and that was kind of a moment where it was really difficult.

“I liked to play games, which was good. The club, really good club as well. I really had a lot of time for Doncaster and everyone up there, it was just the situation at the time that wasn't ideal.”

Ikeme spoke The Yorkshire Post on behalf of Midnite. Midnite, the Principal Partner of Wolverhampton Wanderers for the 2026/27 season, are providing luxury coach travel on the ‘Midnite Express’ for 100 Wolverhampton Wanderers supporters, as they set off on a 130-mile-round trip to watch their beloved Wolves take on the league’s glamour club, Wrexham, this Saturday, November 7.

Fans will be joined on the Express by Wolves club legends, Steve Bull, Carl Ikeme and Matt Jarvis and treated to club-centric quizzes and live Q&As, with exclusive prizes up for grabs.

#1908. The Man Utd change Michael Carrick must make against Aston Villa to keep his job

With JJ Gabriel almost out the door at Old Trafford Manchester United, and Michael Carrick will now be tempted to pin all their hopes on another emerging star in Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old has played himself into first-team contention after a dazzling display off the bench in Tuesday’s comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

While it was Bruno Fernandes’ penalty that sparked the revival and Matheus Cunha’s brace that got them over the line, Lacey’s fearless cameo on the right was the catalyst for change.

Even the perennially reserved Michael Carrick couldn’t hide his delight over the performance, noting the teenager has ‘that bit of mischief’ in his locker that troubled Roma for the final 15 minutes of the game. Lacey ended the contest playing in defence after Cunha’s red card with Carrick jokingly christening him his new right-back.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Lacey’s sharp, perfectly-weighted passing enabled United to get up the pitch with real intent – seldom seen this season. He completed every one of his attempted passes and completed all but one of his duels. Operating in tight spaces just in front of the touchline, his first touches and clever exchanges were on point from the moment he came on. His pass for Cunha’s winner couldn’t have been placed better.

It has been a long time coming for Lacey. Injuries shelved tentative plans for him to make his debut at 16 under Erik ten Hag in 2023 and it was a tough road back from those issues that threatened to halt his progress.

‘Everybody in the world knows about Shea Lacey,’ United’s former Under-21 manager Travis Binnion said last year. ‘So he needs a little bit of fortune, he needs to be patient with himself and everybody else needs to be really patient with him.’ That patience could now be about to pay off.

Whether Tuesday’s win was a turning point or another false dawn for United remains to be seen. Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer led United to delirium-inducing comeback victories over Newcastle United in Atalanta with identical scorelines when the pressure was mounting on their shoulders. Both were gone shortly after.

But with Carrick’s back against the wall, there is the opportunity to roll the dice with Lacey. The Liverpool-born talent thumped home a wonderful strike in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton but has seen just 31 minutes of action off the bench since. Excluding the second-half performance against Roma, United’s attack has lacked any verve or real invention. A change is needed and Lacey will feel this is his chance.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It was on the right where he caused damage midweek with Amad Diallo making way for him after 75 minutes. It had been another disappointing evening for the Ivory Coast international who spurned huge opportunities against Chelsea four days earlier.

Since forcing his way back into the side under Erik ten Hag, Amad has been looked upon as United’s most naturally talented winger. But his goal and assist return has fallen woefully short of expectations. He is now approaching one year without a goal, last finding the back of the net in the 4-4 draw with Bournemouth on 15 December. In that time, he has provided two assists – one on the final day of last season against Brighton and the other for Joshua Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 4-1 humiliation in Como two weeks ago.

His haul of 14 goals during his magnificent campaign with Sunderland in the 2022-23 season is a distant memory. A hat-trick against Southampton in January 2025 helped him to an impressive haul of 11 goals and 10 assists in his first full campaign back in Manchester but seven goal involvements in 40 appearances since the start of the 2025-26 campaign is not good enough.

Wayne Rooney alluded to Amad’s problem midweek and made his case for Lacey getting the nod.

‘Amad does some really good things, but it’s that end product, that is what takes you to the next level,’ he told Amazon Prime. ‘And the glimpses of what I’ve seen from Lacey when he has come on…he has got something in there, that little touch and little pass which United needed to get them over the line in this game.’

The win over Roma has shifted a few clouds amid the gloom hanging over Old Trafford and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa now looks a more inviting environment for Carrick to make the change and put his faith in Lacey.

#1907. The 22s, 10 mad minutes, Chivu’s confusion: DAZN reveal unseen details from Milan-Inter

After AC Milan’s win against Inter, DAZN have published the latest Bordocam episode, offering a complete view of the game.

A fourth win in a row for Milan, the most recent Derby della Madonnina will be remembered fondly for several reasons. Not only was Ricardo Kaka inducted into the Hall of Fame, but the Rossoneri dominated their biggest rivals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As MilanVibes relays from the most recent episode of Bordocam, a behind-the-scenes look at the Derby della Madonnina was offered. Of course, the result will certainly make Rossonero want to watch it back.

First and foremost, it showed the night of the 22s. Starting with Ricardo Kaka’s induction into the Hall of Fame before moving to an encounter between referee Guida and Nicolo Barella, reminding him that Luka Modric would be in the middle with him.

After the first goal, it shows the bench celebrating, but not Mike Maignan or Mario Gila; the former remained in his box, whilst the latter had his shirt replaced. On the Inter bench, there was frustration, and a meeting with Yann Bisseck, who mismarked for the goal.

Arsenal have been closely tracking the progress of Monza star Gustavo Varela are ‘one of the first clubs to enquire’ about a possible transfer deal for the forward, according to reports in Portugal.

Varela was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and moved to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

Monza are languishing down in 18th place in the table, with only two wins to their name, in what has been a difficult start to life on their return to Serie A.

It’s claimed Arsenal are among a host of Premier League clubs to have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

The reigning English champions are said to be in the market for a striker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres badly struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

#1904. Mansfield Town vs Macclesfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:46, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:16

Arriving at One Call Stadium as underdogs, famous giant killers Macclesfield will face League One's Mansfield Town in the FA Cup's first round proper.

The Stags have only been eliminated at this stage in one of the last seven seasons, though the Silkmen are in strong form, despite their lower-division status.

Nigel Clough's Mansfield enjoyed their run to the FA Cup's fifth round in 2025-26, and they will be confident of kicking off their campaign in strong fashion this weekend.

That being said, the Stags have endured a mixed season so far, and head into this clash having won two, drawn two and lost one of their last five games.

Most recently, Clough's side were held to a 0-0 draw by relegation-threatened Wigan Athletic on Tuesday, marking the second consecutive match in which they have failed to score, following a 2-0 defeat to Notts County.

Those blanks have left Mansfield sitting 11th in League One with 19 points from 13 games, though a push for promotion is far from impossible, considering they are just three points behind sixth-placed Reading.

A run in the FA Cup could serve as a morale boost for a playoff charge, and supporters will be expecting to see the Stags progress at One Call Stadium, where they have lost just one of their six league outings this term.

Meanwhile, John Rooney's Macclesfield are best known for knocking out then-holders Crystal Palace in the FA Cup's third round last term, but they will need to navigate a pair of tough tests to make it through to face another Premier League club this time around.

This may be the first round proper, but the National League North side have already beaten Redcar Athletic 2-1, Scarborough 2-1 and Anstey Nomads 3-0 to reach this stage.

Those hard-fought victories have only served to bolster the Silkmen's resolve to prove they are more than a mere novelty, and having downed Bedford 3-0 last weekend - their fourth win in six games - the club will be cautiously optimistic.

That latest success marked a second clean sheet in three matches for Rooney's men, who boast the joint-best defensive record in the sixth tier, having conceded just 11 goals in 13 fixtures.

Macclesfield are also pushing for promotion in the National League North, where they are third with 27 points, a tally that has them just two off top-of-the-table South Shields.

However, the visitors remain significant underdogs, even if they have only tasted defeat once on the road across all competitions this season, winning six times and drawing twice.

Mansfield will be without centre-back Baily Cargill once again due to a hamstring injury, while Kyle Knoyle was forced off against Wigan through injury.

In their absence, Luke Bolton could start alongside Adedeji Oshilaja and Ryan Sweeney in the Stags' defence, flanked by Nathan Moriah-Welsh and Jordan Bowery.

Further forward, Michael Smith and Rhys Oates could lead the attack, platformed by a midfield featuring Louis Reed, George Maris and Elliott Hewitt.

As for Macclesfield, they are missing left-back Brandon Lee as he recovers from a long-term leg injury that has kept him sidelined since last season's FA Cup second round win over Slough in December 2025.

On Saturday, Cameron Borthwick-Jackson could operate on the left of a four-man defence, next to Tom Wilson, Sam Heathcote and Ammar Dyer.

Roberts; Bolton, Oshilaka, Sweeney; Reed; Moriah-Welsh, Maris, Hewitt, Bowery; Smith, Oates

Macclesfield Town possible starting lineup:

Dibble; Dyer, T Wilson, Heathcote, Borthwick-Jackson; Ustabasi, Shrimpton, G Wilson, Kay; Duffy, Elliott

Mansfield may have blanked in their last two matches, but they should have enough to get over the line against a sixth-tier opponent.

Macclesfield are one of the strongest sides in the National League North and could put up a fight, yet it would still come as a surprise to see anything other than a home win on Saturday.

#1900. Liverpool injury, suspension list and return dates for Crystal Palace: Ryan Gravenberch, Hugo Ekitike latest

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:58

Liverpool will look to respond to their latest defeat by beating Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds not only lost 1-0 against Arsenal in the Premier League last weekend, but they also lost 3-2 against Fenerbahce on Wednesday in the Champions League.

Andoni Iraola cannot afford to head into the next international break on the back of a third consecutive loss in all competitions.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace.

Possible return date: November 8 (vs. Crystal Palace)

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, and he has cast doubt on whether the Dutchman will be involved before the international break, though he has not ruled him out of featuring in some capacity against Palace.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

The right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him."

Possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City)

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some time, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The plan was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one]."

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

#1897. Kevin Keegan's iconic Hamburg shirt from 1977 Super Cup against Liverpool sells for £84,500 at auction

Published: 13:58 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:10 EDT, 2 November 2026

Kevin Keegan's iconic 1977 European Super Cup shirt has been sold at auction for a jaw-dropping £84,500.

The 1977 European Super Cup was contested between Liverpool, Keegan's former side, and his new club Hamburg. Despite drawing 1-1 in the first leg, Hamburg lost 6-0 in Keegan's first return to Anfield since his signing.

The much-loved legend's No7 shirt formed part of his former Liverpool team-mate Emlyn Hughes' collection. Hughes, who died in 2004, got it in a swap, and it was estimated at around £2,000 to £3,000 by BUDDS auctioneers.

The sky-blue and white adidas shirt features a v-neck style collar and embroidered badge.

The sale comes just months after the football world was plunged into mourning over the death of Keegan, who was regarded as one of the greatest players of his generation.

Keegan began his playing career at Scunthorpe United in 1968, before Bill Shankly signed him for Liverpool. There, he won seven major trophies including three league titles and one European Cup during a six-year spell.

The 1977 European Super Cup was contested between Liverpool, Keegan's former side, and his new club Hamburg

The much-loved legend's No7 shirt formed part of his former Liverpool team-mate Emlyn Hughes' collection

Ever ambitious, Keegan signed for Hamburg in 1977, and it was during his three-year spell in Germany that the 5ft 7in Englishman earned the nickname the 'Mighty Mouse', winning the league title in 1979 and reaching the 1980 European Cup final, where his side were beaten by Nottingham Forest.

It was also at Hamburg that he confirmed his world-class credentials, winning the Ballon d'Or in 1978 and 1979.

The following year he surprisingly joined Southampton before finishing his playing career with Newcastle, where his love affair with the Geordie fans was born during their 1984 promotion-winning campaign.

Keegan made 63 England appearances and captained his country over 30 times, although his only World Cup was an injury-scarred appearance in 1982.

In 1992, Keegan made his first step into management at his former club Newcastle, guiding them into the Premier League and to within touching distance of the 1995-96 title only to miss out to Manchester United.

After leaving St James' Park in January 1997, a brief stint at Fulham followed before he became England manager in 1999, having initially taken on the job following Glenn Hoddle's departure.

Having overseen a disappointing Euro 2000 campaign, Keegan resigned on the back of defeat by Germany at Wembley Stadium, the last match at the national stadium before it was rebuilt.

After his death, an extraordinary sea of flowers surrounded St James' Park to pay tribute to 'The Messiah' who led their charge back into the top-flight in 1984

After England, he managed Manchester City for four years before returning for a brief spell at Newcastle.

Following his death, an extraordinary sea of flowers surrounded St James' Park to pay tribute to 'The Messiah'.

The club wrote a moving statement at the time, which read: 'We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club's history.

'Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.'

#1896. Kidderminster Harriers v Doncaster Rovers: Respecting the FA Cup is key to Rovers' recent record

Doncaster Rovers have become adept at navigating tricky FA Cup first-round games away at lower-league opposition in Grant McCann’s time. It is just their manager is ready for a home game.

Two years ago the then-League Two side won away at National League side Kettering Town in a first-round tie chosen for television, on their way to a fourth-round exit when finally back on home soil at the hands of eventual winners Crystal Palace.

Then last season, Crewe from the division below were overcome in the first round, en route to a third-round exit against Southampton.

This year, Rovers have been handed a trip to Kidderminster Harriers, two divisions below in mid-table in the National League.

McCann says there is no secret to why they have done so well in these types of ties in recent years, other than paying the competition respect.

“I don't think we do anything different. We always try and approach every game as best we can, given the opposition we're playing against,” he told The Yorkshire Post.

“I don't think there's any real special ingredients behind it.

“You've got to try and pick the best team for the game that's coming up.

“That Kettering game was probably a banana skin. TV cameras there, and we end up scoring a few great goals to win the game.

“The National League's a decent league, it's a strong league this year. I said to the players after the game at Rochdale (won 4-1 in EFL Trophy), this will be harder than that game. Make no mistake about it.”

And on their recent draws, he added: “It would be nice to have a home game. The analysts have shown me that since I've been here, I don't think we've had a home game in the first or second round in four years.

“It would be nice to get through, draw somebody at home, and then see if we can have a little bit of a run at it. But we know it will be a tough game.”

#1895. Former Man Utd chairman slams owners after controversial Avram Glazer comments

Former Manchester United chairman Martin Edwards expects supporters to be furious with Avram Glazer’s comments on the club and has accused the owners of getting their priorities wrong.

The Athletic report that Glazer made a controversial point while speaking to financiers at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London in September.

One of the owners of the Red Devils compared Manchester United to the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys as a brand that will remain commercially successful irrespective of how well they are performing on the pitch.

Edwards, who was chairman of Manchester United from 1980-2003, expects fans to react badly to that sentiment and has encouraged the current owners to train all their focus on improving the team.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘I heard that this morning and I thought “By Jove, what’s the reaction going to be from the supporters?” Supporters don’t want to hear that!’ Edwards said on talkSPORT.

‘Supporters want to hear that you’re winning trophies. They’re not interested in profits or dividends or what people are taking out of the club. They want the club to be successful, they want the best players, they’d rather be spending money on the team than on the new stadium.’

Edwards accepts that running a club the size of Manchester United is a tricky business and owners must satisfy various stakeholders, but he feels the balance is currently off.

‘When I was running United, I always felt I had three responsibilities, really,’ he said. ‘One: in those days we were still developing the ground, so I had to build the ground and develop the ground. Look after the team, which is always the most important. But also, because we were public we had to pay dividends and keep the shareholders happy.

‘It’s a balance. Running a football club is a complete balance, from top to balance. It’s a question of whether you get it right or wrong.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He added: ‘I think it’s quite clear, in my eyes, that the team is the most important element at the moment. You’ve got to get the team right and forget new stadiums if you’re not going to fill them. Get the team winning again and get the supporters behind you. We’re not a united front at the moment.’

The landscape of top flight football has changed considerably since Edwards was in charge at Manchester United and he believes it has not all been for the better.

‘You’ve got owners now who don’t attend games. They put somebody in charge, whatever else,’ he said. ‘Existing owners now, they wouldn’t know who’s in the team.

‘It’s become big business and what you can get out of it. The game has changed and for the older ones of us it’s disappointing, really, the direction it’s gone.’

Looking back to the start of Manchester United’s decline as a title-challenging force in the Premier League, Edwards suggests it was the loss of Alex Ferguson and CEO David Gill in 2013 and Ed Woodward being named as Gill’s replacement.

‘Once Alec and David Gill decided to leave in 2013, that was a huge blow to the club and they’ve never really recovered from that,’ he said.

‘If you wanted to be critical you’d say right from the beginning when they replaced David Gill, they replaced him with not a football man, but a merchant banker.

‘If you’ve got the top of the football chain who’s not converse with football, that does make it difficult. I think that once the mistakes start, they multiply.

‘Recruitment has been a big problem. Look at the players they’ve bought, some of them haven’t been up to the standard. Generally it snowballs. That’s been the problem.

‘Also, have United spent enough money to be able to compete at the top? Manchester City have had a huge advantage in the short-term because they haven’t been sticking to the rules and other people have. That’s given them a huge advantage, so we probably couldn’t have competed with them, but we could certainly have competed with Liverpool and Arsenal and whatever else.’

#1893. ‘Different level’ – William Gallas backs Arsenal star for Real Madrid transfer

William Gallas believes that William Saliba could be tempted to join Real Madrid if the Spanish giants tried to sign the Arsenal defender.

Saliba joined Arsenal in a £27m move from Saint-Etienne in 2019 and has gone on to establish himself as one of the best centre-backs in the league.

The Frenchman was an integral part of Mikel Arteta’s side that won the league title last season, forming a rock-solid partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes at the heart of Arsenal’s defence.

Saliba is under contract at Arsenal until 2030, signing a long-term deal in 2025 after he was heavily linked with Real Madrid.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Gallas still believes he is destined to play for Madrid, and said his fellow countryman would find it hard to turn down a move to a club of that stature.

‘Are Arsenal at a high enough level now that William Saliba would turn down Real Madrid if they came in for him?’ Gallas told SeatPick.

‘I know a lot of people will be mad about what I’m going to say right now but if we are talking about the history of both clubs, Real Madrid and Arsenal, then Real Madrid is Real Madrid. They are on a different level.’

‘The pressure is bigger there. The atmosphere around the club is different. Every game, the fans expect you to win. Every game, the fans expect you to have a great performance. Every season, the fans expect you to win La Liga or to win the Champions League, so it’s a different level.

‘For me, even if their performances at the moment are not the best, and even if they haven’t won the biggest trophies recently, Madrid is Madrid, and I’m telling you, any player who has the opportunity to go to Madrid, they will try to go there, and you can’t blame them. You couldn’t blame a player like Saliba if that is his decision.

After a difficult October, it seems Ruben Amorim will give some of his more prominent AC Milan players a break in the Europa League.

Lorenzo Torriani will replace the suspended Mike Maignan, Luka Modric will be replaced by Ardon Jashari and then there will be other starts for Davide Bartesaghi, Alphadjo Cisse and even ‘the veteran’ Omari Hutchinson.

Sankhoun Diawara could start again, this time in place of Strahinja Pavlovic, and maybe Pervis Estupinan and Filippo Terracciano will start.

Additionally, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda could be seen, with one a possible starter. It seems more likely that it’d be the striker at this moment, though.

#1890. Luton Town vs Forest Green Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 05:05, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:20

Meeting at Kenilworth Road in the FA Cup's first round proper for the second season in a row, Luton Town and Forest Green Rovers will lock horns in a cross-division clash on Saturday.

The Hatters have progressed beyond this stage every year since 2013-14, though the Green have only lost one of their last seven matches.

Jack Wilshere's Luton are in the hunt for promotion from League One, and a strong run in the FA Cup could inspire the team in their push.

The Hatters arrive for Saturday's cup clash unbeaten in five games, winning four on the bounce prior to a 1-1 draw with Huddersfield on Tuesday.

That stalemate has Wilshere's side fourth in the third tier with 24 points after 14 matchdays, just two points behind second-placed Stockport County.

Luton's commendable campaign so far has been built on their attacking prowess, and it is notable that top-of-the-table Huddersfield are the only club to have outscored their tally of 26 goals in League One.

Saturday's hosts will be expecting to progress against their lower-tier opponents, though Wilshere is hoping for a more straightforward victory than last season's 4-3 first-round triumph over Forest Green.

The Hatters raced into a three-goal lead through Lamine Fanne and a Nahki Wells brace that day in October 2025, only to require a 92nd-minute winner from substitute Gideon Kodua after Rovers fought back to 3-3 in the second half.

Forest Green are operating without a permanent manager after Robbie Savage left the club to join Peterborough United last month, though Jonathan Gould is in charge of the National League team on a caretaker basis.

Rovers' owner Dale Vince has said that there is "No vacancy," and the club have won twice, drawn twice and lost just once with the head coach role remaining unfilled.

Most recently, Gould's side followed up their 2-0 victory over Eastleigh with a 2-2 stalemate against Harrogate Town, a particularly frustrating result given the Green held a 2-0 lead at half time.

In the FA Cup's fourth qualifying round, Forest Green were held to a 0-0 draw by Chesham, before thrashing them 5-0 in the replay, courtesy of goals from five different scorers.

The nominal caretaker boss described that attacking performance as a "Tonic," considering the team had suffered from poor finishing across their six-game winless run prior.

Looking ahead to Saturday's first round proper, it remains to be seen whether the visitors can repeat that offensive showcase against higher-tier opposition, though fans will take heart from the fact Rovers have lost on just one of their six away days this term.

Forest Green Rovers form (all competitions):

Luton will be without versatile left-sided defender Kal Naismith, who was forced off after just 17 minutes against Huddersfield.

Filling the gap on Saturday, Wilshere could opt to start Harrison Ashby at right-back and shift Isiah Jones across to the left, with the duo flanking centre-backs George Johnston and Mads Andersen.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Nahki Wells may operate up top, while Kasey Palmer and Tudor Mendel-Idowu line up out wide.

As for Forest Green, they are missing striker Ricardo Rees as he recovers from the cruciate ligament injury he suffered in September.

In his absence, veteran Will Grigg could lead the line this weekend, supported by Kyle McAllister, Kyle Kelly and Bryan Ifeanyi.

Shea; Ashby, Andersen, Johnston, Jones; Walsh; Mendel-Idowu, Donley, Clark, Palmer; Wells

Forest Green Rovers possible starting lineup:

McNicholas; Abrefa, Mabete, McIntyre, Kuemo; Campbell, Clarke; McAllister, Kelly, Ifeanyi; Grigg

Luton are in strong form and have been impressive going forward this season, so expect to see them score more than once on Saturday.

However, Rovers could find the back of the net, too, considering the Hatters have been less than stellar in defence.

#1886. Paris Saint-Germain vs. Troyes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 06 Nov 2026 05:24, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:57

Paris Saint-Germain enter Saturday's gameweek 10 Ligue 1 encounter at Parc des Princes seeking a seventh consecutive league victory and an 11th straight win across all competitions.

The European champions have not dropped points in two months, and Luis Enrique's men are heavy favourites to extend their dominant run against Troyes, who have claimed just one victory in their last seven matches.

PSG enter every Ligue 1 season as overwhelming title favourites, but even many of their own supporters may be surprised by their current winning sequence.

Enrique's team have largely been unremarkable during the first half of recent campaigns before surging into top form after the new year; however, they appear to have found their rhythm considerably earlier this term.

There was a sense of business as usual when PSG suffered a 2-1 defeat at Parc des Princes at the start of September, leaving Les Parisiens with just two points from their opening three matches.

They have since turned the screw, beginning with mid-September's 1-0 success over Brest before victories against Marseille, Le Mans, Strasbourg, Lyon and Le Havre propelled them to the top of the Ligue 1 table.

The Red and Blues could yet be displaced by Lille, who trail by two points, or Lyon or Paris FC, who are both three adrift, but that outcome appears unlikely.

That assessment is reinforced by Troyes' position in the top flight, with 16th-placed ESTAC just one point clear of Le Mans in the automatic relegation places.

On a positive note, Stephane Dumont's team were in the bottom two before last weekend, when Mouhamed Diop and Ismael Boura scored to secure a much-needed victory after exactly two months without one.

However, facing PSG presents an entirely different challenge, and Troyes' return of four points from six alongside consecutive clean sheets could yet prove a false dawn.

A sixth league defeat for ESTAC on Saturday could send them back into the bottom two, although that outcome depends on Le Mans defeating Monaco.

While one result appears likely, given that PSG are unbeaten in their last 10 meetings with Troyes and have won nine, Le Mans must end an eight-match winless sequence against the Monegasques.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (knee) is a long-term absentee for the capital club, while Nuno Mendes (muscle), Marquinhos (thigh) and Ousmane Dembele (thigh) are also sidelined.

Ferran Torres has outscored every teammate in Ligue 1, although the forward has now gone seven matches without scoring for Enrique's men, including four in the league.

The reigning Ligue 1 and Champions League holders were rampant in midweek, demonstrating their wealth of match-winners in a 6-0 thrashing of Villarreal; Fabian Ruiz scored twice, Desire Doue and Senny Mayulu also netted, Maghnes Akliouche registered two assists and Joao Neves contributed a goal and an assist.

ESTAC, meanwhile, have had seven different goalscorers, with Antoine Mille, Diop, Timothe Nkada, Lucas Maronnier, Jeremy Le Douaron, Ismael Boura and Renaud Ripart all finding the net.

Troyes have fewer absentees than their hosts, but Yacouba Kone (knee) will miss Saturday's match; Anis Ouzenadji (knee) is nearing a return but remains doubtful for this weekend.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:

Safonov; Zaire-Emery, Zabarnyi, Pacho, Digne; Neves, Beraldo, Ruiz; Akliouche, Torres, Godts

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz Jr, Iweru; Mille, Karim, Diop; Ifnaoui, Ripart, Nkada

Troyes have restored some confidence with four points and consecutive clean sheets, but containing the European champions represents a considerably greater challenge than their recent assignments.

Fresh from putting six past Villarreal, PSG have enough match-winners to overcome their injury absences and extend their winning sequence with a comfortable home victory.

#1885. Premier League star sparks major police operation after being spotted with a bow and arrows

Newcastle United defender Amar Dedic sparked a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir in Northumberland.

Dedic, who joined Newcastle in a £30 million deal from Benfica in the summer, was reported by a member of the public who saw him and a friend walking with the weapon near the small village of Harlow Hill.

According to the Daily Mail, police dispatched several vehicles to the area, including some that were armed response units.

Dedic and his friend were stopped by police before officers searched a car and seized the bow and arrows.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

After their investigation, officers deemed that there was no threat to the public, although enquiries are ongoing.

Dedic and his friend are said to have fired some arrows while out in the countryside, although it has not been determined what they were aiming at.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

‘Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.’

The Daily Mail adds that Dedic will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident.

#1884. Galli reveals details of Cardinale’s speech at legends dinner: “Heartfelt and sincere”

Before the Inter game, AC Milan invited several legends to a dinner hosted by Gerry Cardinale to honour them.

In recent years, there has maybe been an avoidance of celebrating the club’s history. Iconic players have been overlooked and the past hasn’t been at the forefront. Of course, the present takes precedence, but it’s almost like the rich history of Milan has been overlooked.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been a few nods to the past, as well as a few kits with historic hints. Yet, you’d be lying if you said that the club were completely honouring the legends that had represented them before.

Now, things are seemingly changing. The Hall of Fame presentation was the most public display of affection, but Cardinale also hosted a dinner for the club’s legends. In attendance of the dinner was Filippo Galli, and he’s offered some information on what happened, praising the American for the event, as MilanNews relays from his interview with Gazzetta dello Sport.

“He spoke for a good half hour, and I found it to be heartfelt and sincere. I’d particularly emphasise the mea culpa for the mistakes made. I’d say it’s a good start; his words seemed heartfelt, and not necessary. But there’s still a long way to go.

“He insisted that he will continue to invest. I’d say he understands how soccer works in Italy, compared to the American one, where everything is more relaxed.

“He then spoke kindly of Berlusconi’s career at the club, emphasising, however, that Berlusconi would now be dealing with a changed world, where financial sustainability becomes vital. Now we’re waiting for something to happen…

“Right now, there’s a January transfer window to address, a technical area to sort out and define. There’s a need to establish high-level governance; otherwise the coach will be left alone, and if by chance the results don’t arrive…

“Did this dinner organised by Cardinale surprise me? Actually, yes, we weren’t expecting it. The invitation came from Milan a couple of weeks earlier. For us, these are opportunities to meet up with former teammates, to represent Milan. And this, regardless of who owns the club.”

#1883. Nothing personal says England coach Thomas Tuchel as he overlooks Cole Palmer

The Chelesa playmaker has been left out of the group to face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this month, having pulled out of the last squad through injury.

But there are first call-ups for midfielders Josh King and Jobe Bellingham, the brother of England talisman Jude, whilst the Leeds United pair of James Trafford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin have been retained.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Phil Foden has already learnt the high bar Tuchel has for his squad, and Palmer appears to be the latest star name in his bad books.

But the German insists it is not the case.

“I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception,” said Tuchel despite his pointed comments during the last camp about how many internationals Palmer had been unavailable for.

“I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary.

“If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

“So it’s not personal, and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country. But the competition is on, and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.

“The door is always open, but nothing has changed.”

Palmer was one of five withdrawals ahead of the last camp, along with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford. Of them, only Arsenal midfielder Rice is in the current squad.

Palmer has only won five caps since scoring in the 2024 European Championship final.

The younger Bellingham has never played in the Premier League after leaving Sunderland for Borussia Dortmund two summers ago but has established himself as an important player in the Bundesliga.

He and King have benefited from the absence through injury of Alex Scott, and the fact Mainoo only returned to Manchester United's starting XI on Tuesday.

Dean Henderson returns after injury, along with former Leeds loanees Djed Spence and Ben White.

White made himself unavailable following the 2022 World Cup after a reported disagreement with Gareth Southgate's No 2 Steve Holland.

He made himself available once Tuchel took over, and made his return as a 69th-minute substitute against Uruguay in March.

He was booed onto the field that night, and even scoring England's goal in a 1-1 draw did not win over the Wembley crowd.

"We were not happy about this," said Tuchel. "We could understand the disappointment of the fans with what happened before but I think this is expressed now and this should be a closed book.

“I think everyone could see the investment of Ben, the quality of Ben and how he presented himself in the March camp before the World Cup.

“He did excellently, scored for us and then I think he committed a foul and we conceded.

“It was very eventful, not so easy to come back. When I speak to him, I always feel the hunger to come back, the excitement.

“He is the standout player for Arsenal in a position (right-back) where we struggle with injuries somehow and we have a lot of changes.

“Trevoh Chalobah is not in camp so that makes maybe Jarell Quansah half a full-back and half a centre-back in camp and gives Ben the opportunity to impose himself again.

“He deserves to open a new chapter, he deserves positive feedback from the crowd.

“We want everyone to be supported. This is what helps the team.”

England play at home to Croatia on Thursday, and are in Madrid the following Sunday for their final group match of the competition.

SQUAD: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Dean Henderson (Crystal Palace); Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Marc Guehi (Man City), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal); Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Josh King (Fulham), James Garner (Everton), Elliot Anderson (Man City), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal); Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea).
